## Integration batch A: sessions 196, 202 and 195 land together, and ADR-092's one predicted collision is settled by first-writer-wins (2026-08-25, integration session)

**THE REGISTRY IS 64 OF 111 AND 64 WAS RECOMPUTED FROM `TABLE_KEYS.length` RATHER THAN ADDED UP FROM THE THREE BRANCHES.** At **1 `root`, 26 `owned`, 11 `derived` and 26 `firm`**, so **38 of the 64 are reachable through the scoped accessor** and the other 47 tables through neither. **No ADR, no session number, no migration, no new document; an integration transcribes nothing and rules nothing.**

**THE PER-SESSION COUNT IS SIX, ZERO AND TWO, AND THE ZERO IS THE POINT.** [Session 196](sessions/2026-08-25-session-196.md) registered six -- `payout_requests`, `payout_transfers`, `wallet_entries`, `wallet_withdrawals`, `wallet_spend_limits` and `wallet_dormancy`. [Session 202](sessions/2026-08-25-session-202.md) registered **none**, because all four tables it claimed are 196's four and 196 merged first. [Session 195](sessions/2026-08-25-session-195.md) registered two, `plans` and `passkeys`. **56 to 62 to 62 to 64.**

**[ADR-092](decisions/ADR-092.md) SECTION 8 ITEM 4'S ONE NAMED INTERSECTING PAIR IS RESOLVED THE WAY THE RULING SAYS AND NOT BY JUDGEMENT.** The owner is the TABLE, the first writer wins, a registration is never re-argued: 196's four declarations and 196's four `why` fields stand whole and 202's four rows come out whole. **Nothing was merged, averaged or picked between.** Both texts were read before either was dropped, which is the check the rule needs and does not itself perform.

**THE TWO SESSIONS AGREE, AND THE AGREEMENT WAS MEASURED RATHER THAN ASSUMED.** All four tables are `class: 'owned'`, `column: 'identity_id'`, `nullable: false` in both transcriptions, and the four `pgTable` declarations are **byte-identical in code** on the two branches, differing only in comment and `why` prose. Two sessions reading [`0011`](../packages/db/migrations/0011_wallet.sql) independently, with no roster and no coordination, produced the same column sets, the same types and the same tenancy. **There is no disagreement for the founder to rule on**, which is a different and better outcome than a disagreement resolved by a merger.

## Tranche B integration: five transcription branches land as one, then tranche A lands first and the `plans` collision is settled by dropping session 203's copy, registry 80 of 111 (2026-08-25, session 204)

**FIVE OF FIVE, MERGED IN THE DISPATCHED ORDER, THEN `origin/main` MERGED A SIXTH TIME AFTER TRANCHE A OVERTOOK THIS BRANCH.** [Session 198](sessions/2026-08-25-session-198.md)'s M10 three, [session 203](sessions/2026-08-25-session-203.md)'s M21 two, [session 199](sessions/2026-08-25-session-199.md)'s M13 five, [session 201](sessions/2026-08-25-session-201.md)'s M18 three and [session 200](sessions/2026-08-25-session-200.md)'s M17 four. **The registry reaches 80 of 111**, at **1 root, 34 owned, 14 derived and 31 firm**, so **49 of the 80 are reachable through the scoped accessor**. **No ADR, no migration, no new document and no transcription**: an integration session rules nothing, and this one wanted no ADR number, which was the stop condition it never reached.

**`pnpm run typecheck` WAS RUN AFTER EACH OF THE SIX MERGES AND NOT ONLY AT THE END**, exit 0 with zero `error TS` every time. That is what makes the table below a record rather than a reconstruction: a tail-splice is caught at the merge that caused it, so the bisect never had to run.

**The arithmetic is the check and it is stated rather than implied.** Tranche B alone is 56 + 3 + 2 + 5 + 3 + 4 = **73**. Tranche A took `main` to **64**, its eight being M05's six, M04's `passkeys` and `plans`, with M20's four rebasing out under first-writer-wins. **The intersection of the two tranches is exactly one table, `plans`**, so the merged registry is 64 + 17 - 1 = **80**, and the suite is 85 + 16 = **101**. Read back off the merged tree: `TABLE_KEYS` **80**, `SCOPE_RULES` **80**, `SQL_NAME` **80**, `pgTable` declarations **80**, duplicate keys **0**.

**THE `plans` COLLISION BECAME REAL AND WAS SETTLED THE WAY ADR-092 SAYS, NOT BY MERGING THE TWO COPIES.** [ADR-092](decisions/ADR-092.md) section 8 item 4 named one intersecting pair (`M5-1` and `M20-a`); this is the second, found after dispatch. **`main` carried M04's copy first, so M04's stays and session 203's was DROPPED** from [`schema.ts`](../packages/db/src/schema.ts), from [`scope.ts`](../packages/db/src/scope.ts)'s imports, `TABLES` and `SCOPE_RULES`, and from `SQL_NAME` in the suite. `plans` now appears **exactly once in each of those five sites**, and the surviving `why` is session 195's. **The failure mode if it had been merged instead of dropped is `TS1117`, which is loud, and it was never reached.**

**THE AGREEMENT WAS VERIFIED AT BOTH SOURCES BEFORE THE DROP, NOT ASSUMED.** Both sessions declare `plans` **`firm`**, both give no scope column and say there is no correct one, and both give the same four reasons in different words: the catalogue's root has no identity column, the link runs the other way (a version names its plan, an account names its version), `is_active` delists and never deletes, and it is `plan_versions`' reason one hop up. **Two sessions that never spoke reached the same ruling, so there was nothing to escalate and the registration was not re-argued.** Had they named a different class or scope column, that would have been the founder's question rather than this session's, and it would have been reported instead of resolved.

**EVERY RESOLUTION WAS STRUCTURAL AND NONE WAS A HUNK-LEVEL KEEP-BOTH.** Five of the six conflicted textually in all five files. Each of the three code files was rebuilt from **one side's whole copy** and the other's **WHOLE declarations** re-appended, after asserting the incoming branch byte-identical to its base from its first declaration to its last. **On the tranche A merge the direction was deliberately inverted**: the files were rebuilt from **`main`'s** copy rather than this branch's, precisely so that M04's `plans` is the copy that survives, and this branch's sixteen non-`plans` declarations were appended to it. The hazard is measured rather than feared: every `pgTable` ends with the same `createdAt` / `updatedAt` / `});` tail, so git aligns the hunk on lines two unrelated tables merely happen to share, each side ends MID-DECLARATION, and a keep-both splices one table's columns into another's object literal.

**ONE LIFT WAS REFUSED RATHER THAN TRUNCATED, AND THAT REFUSAL IS WHY THE DECLARATION IS WHOLE.** [Session 199](sessions/2026-08-25-session-199.md)'s `analytics_snapshots` uses the three-argument `pgTable` form for its composite primary key and closes on a bare `);` where every other declaration closes on `});`. The splitter ran off the end and **threw instead of ending the declaration at the wrong line**. **A resolver that had silently taken the last `});` it found would have produced exactly the splice this session existed to avoid, and it would have COMPILED**, because what follows a truncated declaration is another valid one.

**THE REGISTRY SIZE IS A LITERAL IN SIX PLACES, NOT FIVE, AND EVERY ONE WAS RECOMPUTED FROM `TABLE_KEYS.length` RATHER THAN INCREMENTED.** The sixth is [`schema.ts`](../packages/db/src/schema.ts)'s drifted-table sentence, which moves only when a registered table carries a later `ADD COLUMN`. **Both tranches moved it and each knew only its own half**: tranche A made it NINE for `payout_requests`, tranche B made it NINE for `promotional_credit_grants`, and **the merged answer is TEN carrying both**. That was **derived** by replaying every `ALTER TABLE` across all 47 migrations with the suite's own multiline match rather than taken from either side: **ten registered tables carry `ADD COLUMN` and ZERO carry `DROP COLUMN`, `ALTER COLUMN` or `RENAME`**, so [ADR-094](decisions/ADR-094.md)'s closed vocabulary still refuses nothing that is registered. **Two sides each incrementing a count to the same number is the shape that merges green and wrong**, and deriving it is the only thing that catches it.

**ONE STALE FIGURE THAT BELONGED TO NO MERGED SESSION WAS CORRECTED AND IS NAMED RATHER THAN QUIET.** The `` `identity_links` IS ONE OF THE NN `` sentence is 111 minus the registry size and arrived on `92ea3d9` reading **58** where the tree carried 56 and the figure should have been 55, disagreeing with `the other 55` two lines above it. [Session 203](sessions/2026-08-25-session-203.md) caught the same thing from its own side. Both now derive from the one number.

**THE SEVEN DELIBERATE REFUSALS ALL SURVIVE ALL SIX MERGES, CHECKED BY NAME AFTER EVERY ONE**, each at zero occurrences in `TABLES` and zero in `SCOPE_RULES`: `identity_links`, `attributions`, `affiliate_commissions`, `dedupe_matches`, `otp_challenges`, `trading_calendar` and `competitor_plan_models`. **`identity_links` still carries no `pgTable` declaration at all**, which is session 192's stronger form of the refusal and was not "fixed" here; `affiliate_commissions` stays out because `DerivedRule.via` is typed `TableKey` and cannot name the unregistered `attributions`, and **no merge, in either tranche, made that registrable**.

**`CI-06u` CAUGHT THE KEEP-BOTH HAZARD IN THE DOCUMENTS RATHER THAN THE CODE, TWICE.** Keep-both is right for an APPENDED section and wrong for a KEYED registry row, and both kinds live in [`sessions/README`](sessions/README.md). Sessions 198 to 201 each struck their own claim row in place, so the two sides of the hunk held one key in two states and keeping both made the register answer _has 198 been written_ with yes and no at once; the tranche A merge did the same for 202. **The struck `WRITTEN` row was kept in every case and the stale `CLAIMED` duplicate dropped**, and no row's text was edited. All of 194 to 203 now read struck, once each, in numeric order.

**The position:** `pnpm run typecheck` exit 0 with **zero `error TS`**; [`scoped-db.test.ts`](../packages/db/test/scoped-db.test.ts) **101**; `pnpm run gates` <!--gen:gate_count-->32<!--/gen--> of <!--gen:gate_count-->32<!--/gen-->; `pnpm run verify` exit 0. **No session's STATE section or log was edited**, all nine carried through the six merges untouched, and nothing needed a file outside the fence. **`E2` READ REMAINS PENDING on the sixteen money-path tables this branch adds** and on the sixty-four before them, which this session neither discharges nor narrows.

## M02's seven tables enter the transcription, and the one plan that is not approved does not reach any rule written here (2026-08-25, session 205)

**Seven of seven, and nothing had been claimed by a sibling.** `account_status_history`, `platform_account_refs`, `provisioning_queue`, `platform_entitlements` (all [`0007`](../packages/db/migrations/0007_accounts.sql)), `ingest_files`, `raw_ingest_rows` (both [`0013`](../packages/db/migrations/0013_ingest.sql)) and `reconciliations` ([`0014`](../packages/db/migrations/0014_marks.sql)) are in [`schema.ts`](../packages/db/src/schema.ts) and [`scope.ts`](../packages/db/src/scope.ts). **80 of 111 becomes 87 of 111**, 33 `firm` and 54 reachable, every figure recomputed from `TABLE_KEYS.length`. **Three migrations for one module** is M2's shape rather than a mis-derivation: the provisioning half sits in the accounts file, the ingest half in `0013`, and the reconciliation half beside `daily_marks`.

**THE PREMISE WAS VERIFIED BEFORE A LINE WAS TRANSCRIBED, AND IT HOLDS.** [M02](plans/M02-rithmic-bridge.md) is the ONE plan in the corpus that is not `approved`, held at `review` by [ADR-005](decisions/ADR-005.md) pending the Rithmic vendor call. Both stop conditions were checked rather than assumed. **All six schema deltas `SD-M2-01` to `SD-M2-06` are already folded into merged migrations**, checked one at a time against the migration set, so there is no table in the slice whose `CREATE TABLE` is unmerged -- `SD-M2-02`'s word _"new"_ for `platform_account_refs` is the plan's, written before the reconciliation landed it. **And not one of the sixteen `V-M2-nn` rows changes a tenancy column or a join path.** Twelve move the wire format, the parser, cadence, corrections, sandbox and streaming. The four carrying `Blast: model` were read individually: `V-M2-05` lands on the already-registered `daily_marks`; **`V-M2-09` is the closest and it stops one column short**, moving the BILLING UNIT while `platform_entitlements.account_id` stays `NOT NULL` and `platform_user_ref` stays `text NULL` with no foreign key; `V-M2-10` would change `platform_account_refs`' PRIMARY KEY, which under this rule is the burn rather than the tenancy; `V-M2-11` would empty two tables of rows and change no rule about whose rows they are. **What is provisional in these tables is their CONTENT and not their CLASS**, and the transcription says so at the point of use.

**FIVE `derived` THROUGH `accounts` IN ONE HOP AND TWO `firm`.** `ingest_files` is firm because a vendor file carries rows for every account that traded the session, its only foreign key points at ITSELF, and the tenancy runs the other way -- `fills`, `raw_ingest_rows` and `reconciliations` all point IN. The quarantine machine is why the grain is the file: a `quarantined` file has committed no downstream rows, so at the moment the row matters most there is no account row anywhere to reach it through.

**`raw_ingest_rows` CARRIES THE SLICE'S FINDING, AND THE WRONG RULE IS GREEN.** The forward derivation through the firm `ingest_files` is the trap [ADR-094](decisions/ADR-094.md) already names and the bounded chain assertion catches it. **The REVERSE edge is worse and nothing in the package catches it**: `fills.raw_row_id bigint NOT NULL REFERENCES raw_ingest_rows(id)` is a declared foreign key in the direction the derived-rule assertion accepts, so `derived via fills, localColumn id, foreignColumn raw_row_id, semi-join` was **SEEDED AND WATCHED PASSING -- `typecheck` exit 0 and the suite GREEN at 108 of 108** -- rendering `exists (select 1 from "fills" where ("fills"."raw_row_id" = "raw_ingest_rows"."id" and exists (select 1 from "accounts" ...)))`. It answers a DIFFERENT QUESTION: which raw rows produced a fill on this person's accounts, rather than whose raw row this is. Only some raw rows become fills, and an EOD balance row, an unparsed row and **every row of a quarantined file** become none -- so the reading silently drops exactly the rows a dispute is argued from. **That is [session 202](sessions/2026-08-25-session-202.md)'s `wallet_entries` finding recurring on a different table: the green suite is not the check, the reading of the DDL is.**

**Two more seeds watched failing loudly.** `reconciliations` declared `derived via ingestFiles` fails the bounded chain assertion **by name**; `provisioning_queue.payload_hash` deleted from the transcription fails the per-table drift assertion with the column named. Both files were restored and `git status --porcelain` reported clean before the next command ran.

**[ADR-094](decisions/ADR-094.md)'S FOLD APPLIES NOTHING TO ANY OF THE SEVEN**, re-derived over all 47 migrations with the suite's own multiline match: no `ALTER TABLE` names any of them in any shape, so all seven are among the 99 undrifted. **The drifted-table sentence was DERIVED rather than left alone**, because it is the one number nothing in the suite checks: replaying `ADD COLUMN` across the whole registry returns **exactly ten**, and **zero** carry a refused verb, so the sentence stays **TEN** and now reads _of the eighty-seven_.

**`payload_hash` and `sha256` are `bytea` CUSTOM TYPES and not `text`**, on the file's own rule, and two enums join from [`0001`](../packages/db/migrations/0001_extensions_and_enums.sql): `provisioning_status`, whose `confirmed_inferred` is a distinct state rather than a synonym, and `ingest_file_status`. The binding rule over the pair -- `set_risk` may never reach `confirmed_inferred` -- stays a table CHECK and is not restated as a type.

**ONE NON-EDIT IS REPORTED RATHER THAN MADE**, on [session 203](sessions/2026-08-25-session-203.md)'s precedent. Registering these two ingest tables satisfies [`schema.ts`](../packages/db/src/schema.ts)'s _"only when"_ condition for `daily_marks.ingest_file_id` and for `fills.ingest_file_id` and `fills.raw_row_id`, whose comments read _"not one of this file's tables"_ and are wrong after this branch merges. `.references()` is compared by nothing in this package and touching a table that is not this slice's is the tail-splice hazard tranche 1 paid for, so all three are left and named.

## `P4-d`: Fastify enters the catalog and the route registry is a DIRECTORY LISTING, so the fifteen route slices behind it stop being serial (2026-08-25, session 209)

**[ADR-100](decisions/ADR-100.md), `accepted`. THIS REPOSITORY NOW ANSWERS AN HTTP REQUEST.** `apps/api` composes route modules and serves [API_CONTRACT section 9](architecture/API_CONTRACT.md)'s liveness row, and both of ADR-083's deployments were watched doing it over a real socket.

**THE DELIVERABLE IS THE SHAPE, WHICH IS WHAT `P4-d`'s ROW SAID IT WAS.** That row's money column is the only one in [P4](plans/P4-portal-and-site.md) section 8 carrying a consequence instead of a yes or a no: _"the registry's SHAPE decides whether M19's seven route slices serialize."_ **A route module is one file under `apps/api/src/routes/` that default-exports `defineRoutes({ name, routes })`, `discoverRouteModules` reads the directory and imports every `.ts` file in sorted order, and no file outside that directory imports anything inside it.** So a slice that adds a route **adds one file and edits nothing another slice edits**, and the **fifteen** slices [P4](plans/P4-portal-and-site.md) section 9 rows behind that file -- `P4-f`, M03's two, M05's two, M16's three and [M19's seven](sessions/2026-08-24-session-168.md) -- touch fifteen disjoint paths and merge in any order.

**`apps/api/src/routes/index.ts`, WHICH SECTION 9 NAMES AS A BARRIER, IS NOT CREATED AND IS NOT NEEDED.** There is nothing for a later slice to register into. That is the barrier removed rather than scheduled, and it is the largest single lever this phase had on every later phase's concurrency.

**THE THREE PROPERTIES AN ARRAY GIVES FREE WERE BOUGHT BACK RATHER THAN ASSUMED**, each watched in [`registry.test.ts`](../apps/api/test/registry.test.ts): `defineRoutes` is typed `(m: RouteModule) => RouteModule` so `tsc` reports a malformed module **in the module's own file**; discovery **throws** on any `.ts` file that is not a valid module and on a name that is not its filename stem; and `compose` refuses a duplicate `METHOD /path` across the module set **before** the surface filter. **That third one is strictly stronger than an array**, which would have merged both copies and left Fastify to refuse the second registration at startup.

**A MODULE DECLARES A PATH AND NEVER A SURFACE, AND THERE IS DELIBERATELY NO FIELD FOR ONE.** `compose` classifies every declared path with [`surface.ts`](../apps/api/src/surface.ts)'s `classifyPath` and registers only what this process serves, so [ADR-083](decisions/ADR-083.md) section 4's 404 stays the router's. **Watched in two processes composing the SAME module set**: `GET /api/v1/internal/jobs` answered **404 `application/problem+json`** on `api` and **200** on `api-admin`, and the public process logged `"registered":["GET /health"],"withheld":["GET /internal/jobs"]`. No permission check ran on either side.

**THE `VG-12` ADMISSION IS 46 PACKAGES AND THE CHECK WAS RUN RATHER THAN WAVED THROUGH.** Closure **233 to 279**, 0 removed; **46 of 46** resolve to a registry entry carrying a `sha512` integrity hash and none to a tarball, a git reference or a link; **zero** declare `preinstall`, `install` or `postinstall`, so `onlyBuiltDependencies: []` is unchanged; `pnpm audit --audit-level=low` exit 0. `5.12.1` is the version [ADR-083](decisions/ADR-083.md) section 5 measured and is also what the registry resolves as latest.

**`VG-3` AND `VG-6` MOVE OFF THE LOCKFILE ONTO `scopedDb` NAMED UNDER `apps/api/src`, AND THE GATE WAS WATCHED FAILING ON THE GOOD NEWS FIRST.** `CI-06/vg-inventory` went to **29 of 30** on the catalog commit, naming both rows, **before either cell moved**. The new artifact is [API_CONTRACT section 1](architecture/API_CONTRACT.md)'s own mechanism for what both rows are about -- _"Every authenticated handler resolves the caller to an identity and reads through `scopedDb(identity)`"_ -- and a lockfile key could only ever say a server was possible. The probe was watched firing on a seeded `scopedDb` and **not** firing on `scopedDbFixture`.

**THE FALSIFY SEED BROKE, AND THAT IS THE DESIGN WORKING RATHER THAN A DEFECT.** [`falsify.mjs`](../scripts/corpus/falsify.mjs)'s `CI-06/vg-inventory` seed planted a `fastify` key while both rows waited on one; with a real key present the anchor stopped existing and the case **threw** instead of passing, taking `pnpm run falsify` to 1 problem. **A harness that had matched loosely would have appended a second key and reported green.** The seed moved onto the live artifact and scope cases went **69 to 70**.

**TWO FINDINGS ARE REPORTED AND NOT REPAIRED, AND NEITHER IS THIS FENCE'S.**

- **NO `start` SCRIPT IN THIS ESTATE HAS EVER RUN.** `node --experimental-strip-types` resolves a specifier to the file it names and does not map `./x.js` onto `x.ts`. `apps/api`, `apps/admin` and `apps/worker` all declare that runtime and all three die with `ERR_MODULE_NOT_FOUND` on their own first relative import. **[ADR-083](decisions/ADR-083.md) is not edited and its ruling 3 is not weakened**: its section 5 measured a scratch program whose specifiers matched, and this tree's convention was not in that measurement. **The repair was EXECUTED in a scratch copy to prove it sufficient** -- `./x.js` to `./x.ts` plus `allowImportingTsExtensions` in the tsconfig, without which `tsc` reports `TS5097` -- and `apps/api/tsconfig.json` is outside this fence while the other two deployables are outside it entirely.
- **[ADR-085](decisions/ADR-085.md)'s SIGNED CLAUSE IS THE EIGHTH OF THE DRIFTED-ENUMERATION CLASS [ADR-099](decisions/ADR-099.md) section 4 named.** It says `29 of 29` where the tree is 30 of 30, and says the gate is watched failing when a real `fastify` key is seeded, which now reopens nothing. **Its ruling is untouched and correct.** A signed entry moves by a superseding ADR, so `CI-06/vg-inventory/fastify-near-miss` is **retained verbatim** rather than deleted or repointed, because that clause cites it by name.

**THE PLAN DISAGREES WITH ITSELF IN TWO PLACES AND BOTH ARE REPORTED RATHER THAN RESOLVED SILENTLY.** `P4-d`'s Contents cell lists no ADR file while rowing `ALLOCATION` (its row) and `INDEX` (its row), which on this tree is the generated `adr_count` span and nothing else, so both cells hold nothing unless an ADR lands; and section 11 rule 8 names `P4-d` by name as owing one. And that cell rows `gates.mjs` and not `falsify.mjs`, while **section 9, which section 8 says is the table to read**, rows `falsify.mjs` for `P4-d` -- and it had to be edited, because the seed inside it breaks on this slice's own artifact.

**The position:** `pnpm run typecheck` exit 0 with **zero `error TS`**; `apps/api` **10 tests to 37**; the suite **1,611 to 1,638 passed / 1 skipped** over 109 files; [`scoped-db.test.ts`](../packages/db/test/scoped-db.test.ts) **101**, untouched; **8 of 8** invariants with `RI-09` needing no change; **30 of 30** gates; `pnpm run verify` **exit 0**; `pnpm run falsify` 30 gates clean-and-dirty over **70** scope cases and 10 loader cases; `falsify:ci CI-01` **12 of 12** with `git status --porcelain` empty immediately after. **`0048` stays free, no `SD-nn` moves, and nothing on the money path was touched.**

## `derived` is refused on a row that owns its identity and refused again on a nullable edge, and the trap `scope.ts` names in its own header turned out to be writable (2026-08-25, session 212)

**[ADR-101](decisions/ADR-101.md) lands at `status: proposed` with the approval line UNSIGNED. MONEY PATH, and the `E2` line-by-line read is owed on it.** [Session 202](sessions/2026-08-25-session-202.md) reported two `derived` rules the registry could write and should not, and reported them rather than repairing them because a transcription rules nothing. **Both were reproduced before either was ruled on, and a third was found that nobody had.**

**RULED, and the ruling is FIVE ASSERTIONS rather than a paragraph:**

> **`derived` is unavailable where the row itself declares a column `REFERENCES identities(id)`.** A derivation on such a row can only answer a DIFFERENT question from the one that column already answers, and it answers it by returning rows rather than by raising.
>
> **`derived` may not traverse a NULLABLE edge.** There is no admissible reading of one: the database has declared the relationship optional, and a scope rule may not answer _"whose row is this"_ with silence on the rows where it is absent.
>
> **`DerivedRule` gains NO `nullable` field. [`OwnedRule.nullable`](../packages/db/src/scope.ts) is CHECKED against the DDL instead, for the first time.**

**[`packages/db/src/scope.ts`](../packages/db/src/scope.ts) IS NOT EDITED and no table's rows are touched** -- `git status --porcelain packages/db/src` reports zero on the branch that carries it. That is deliberate twice over: a comment naming the refusal would be the prose [ADR-042](decisions/ADR-042.md) refuses, and [sessions 205 through 208](sessions/README.md) are transcribing into that file concurrently.

**THREE WRONG RULES WERE SEEDED ON `main` AT `fe05a2e` AND THE WHOLE ESTATE ACCEPTED ALL THREE**, `pnpm run typecheck` at exit 0 with **zero `error TS`** and [`scoped-db.test.ts`](../packages/db/test/scoped-db.test.ts) at **101 of 101** on each:

| Seeded rule                                                                   | What it answers instead                            |
| ----------------------------------------------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------- |
| `walletEntries` `derived` via `ledgerTransactions` on `ledger_transaction_id` | whose ledger accounts appear on this transaction   |
| `walletWithdrawals` `derived` via `riskFlags` on `freeze_flag_id`             | the CORRECT identity's FROZEN withdrawals only     |
| `sessions` `derived` via `identitySignals` on `device_fingerprint_id`         | whoever SHARES A DEVICE, on the rows that name one |

**THE THIRD IS THE ONE THAT DECIDES THE SHAPE OF THE REMEDY AND NEITHER SESSION 202 NOR THE DISPATCH HAD IT.** [`scope.ts`](../packages/db/src/scope.ts) names that exact traversal in its own first twenty lines, as one of three reasons the registry is declared rather than derived. **The file's own named trap is writable as a rule and the estate stays green, which is the argument for a mechanical instrument stated as a measurement rather than as a principle.**

**EVERY EXISTING MECHANISM AGREES WITH ALL THREE AND NONE OF THEM IS DEFECTIVE.** [Session 188](sessions/2026-08-25-session-188.md)'s bounded-chain assertion asks whether a chain terminates and all three do; the derived-FK assertion asks whether the edge is declared and all three are; the `traversal` assertion asks whether the hop is single-valued and all three are; `scopePredicate` renders SQL, binds the identity and is not a table scan. **None of them was ever asking whether the identity it terminates at is the RIGHT one.**

**CLAUSE 1 DOES NOT CATCH THE `sessions` SEED, WHICH IS WHY THERE ARE TWO CLAUSES.** `sessions` carries no identity column of its own, so the candidate ruling as dispatched refuses it not at all and **clause 2 fires alone**. A ruling that had adopted only the candidate would have closed two of the three holes and read as if it had closed all three.

**MEASURED AGAINST ALL EIGHTY RULES BEFORE IT WAS ADOPTED, AND IT TURNS NOTHING RED.** The registry at `fe05a2e` is **80 of 111** at 1 root / 34 owned / 14 derived / 31 firm. **Clause 1 refuses 0 of 14. Clause 2 refuses 0 of 14. Clause 3 passes 34 of 34.** There is no exemption list because there is nothing to exempt, and a mechanism carrying an exemption facility would be carrying a facility for its own future weakening.

**CLAUSE 2 IS ALREADY THE REGISTRY'S PRACTICE, ARGUED EIGHT TIMES IN PROSE AND ENFORCED NOWHERE.** `risk_flags`, `coupons`, `coupon_redemptions`, `psp_webhook_events`, `account_adjustments`, `journal_entries`, `promotional_credit_grants` and `wallet_withdrawals` each refuse a derivation on exactly this ground, each naming the column and the rows it would drop. **Eight authors reached the same conclusion independently and the ninth wrote the rule anyway, because nothing between them was a control.**

**`OwnedRule.nullable` WAS STATED BY 34 RULES, READ BY NOTHING AND CHECKED BY NOTHING.** [`scoped-db.ts:84-89`](../packages/db/src/scoped-db.ts) declines it in its own comment -- _"Adding `IS NOT NULL` here would look careful and assert nothing"_ -- and `grep -n nullable` over the suite returned **zero** across 101 tests. **The field was a comment with a type for as long as the registry has existed**, which is the whole argument against giving `DerivedRule` a second one, and clause 3 goes the other way for four lines.

**A COMPILE-TIME REFUSAL IS IMPOSSIBLE FOR CLAUSE 1 AND THE REASON IS STRUCTURAL RATHER THAN A MATTER OF EFFORT.** The predicate is a fact about the DDL, `tsc` cannot read a migration, and the only encoding would be a second statement of the fact in TypeScript -- which is [ADR-092](decisions/ADR-092.md) section 5's measured hazard plus [session 145](sessions/2026-08-23-session-145.md)'s rule asserted against itself. **This is [ADR-084](decisions/ADR-084.md)'s own division of labour: totality is a compile error because `keyof` can see it, and which class a rule may take is a fact about the DDL, so it lands on the assertion side.**

**A LIVE FINDING IS RECORDED AND DELIBERATELY NOT REPAIRED.** `no firm table carries a column referencing identities, so the class is not hiding one` states a claim that is **FALSE about this tree** and is green because its reader stops at `CREATE TABLE`: `admin_actions.on_behalf_of_identity_id uuid NULL REFERENCES identities(id)` is `ALTER`-added in [`0043`](../packages/db/migrations/0043_admin_attributed_actions.sql), and folded over all 47 migrations it is the **only** one of the 31 firm tables that reaches `identities` directly. **`admin_actions` is correctly `firm`**, so pointing the assertion at the fold turns it RED on a row nothing is wrong with, and the green then requires a restatement of what the `firm` class PROMISES -- a ruling about a different class. **The remedy is one line and is written out**: the assertion takes `identityColumnsOf(...)`, which session 212 adds. **The `owned` column assertion has the same reader and is sound only because zero of the 34 `owned` columns is `ALTER`-added, measured rather than assumed.**

**EACH SEED WAS WATCHED BEING REFUSED BY THE CLAUSE THAT NAMES IT, AND EACH CLAUSE WAS MUTATION-CHECKED.** Seed 1 fails clause 1 alone quoting `[ 'identity_id' ]` back; seed 2 fails clauses 1 and 2, the second quoting `freeze_flag_id uuid NULL REFERENCES risk_flags(id)`; seed 3 fails clause 2 alone; a flipped `ledgerAccounts` flag fails clause 3. **Removing the `PRIMARY KEY` leg of the nullability reader fails on `wallet_dormancy` by name**, which is [session 202](sessions/2026-08-25-session-202.md)'s landmine arriving as a mutation result, and **stopping the definition fold at `CREATE TABLE` fails on `sessions`** from the assertion that binds the two folds together.

**THE REFUSAL COULD PASS BY READING NOTHING, AND ONE OF THE FIVE ASSERTIONS EXISTS ONLY TO REFUSE THAT.** Clause 1 passes today by finding nothing on fourteen tables, so a reader that silently stopped matching would find nothing on all eighty and look identical. `the identity-column reader finds the column every owned rule names` fails **34 times** in that case, once per `owned` rule.

**THE APPROVAL CLAUSE IS A COMMAND RATHER THAN A COUNT**, on the seven signed clauses that have drifted on their enumeration while the ruling held. The counts above are true at `fe05a2e` and **will** go stale as the registry grows from 80 toward 111; nothing asks a signature to stand behind them.

**THE ENTRY IS `ADR-101` AND IT WAS `ADR-100` UNTIL THE MERGE.** [Session 209](sessions/2026-08-25-session-209.md) wrote [ADR-100](decisions/ADR-100.md) and merged it at `4fd4a8a` while this branch was open; `100` was the lowest free number when this session read [ALLOCATION](decisions/ALLOCATION.md) at `fe05a2e` and both sessions took it, which is [ADR-089](decisions/ADR-089.md)'s collision a third time. **The renumber happened at the merge, which is the only point at which it could**, and its scope was enumerated by `grep -rn 'ADR-100'` over the whole diff rather than from memory -- including **three comment blocks in [`scoped-db.test.ts`](../packages/db/test/scoped-db.test.ts)**, which no earlier renumber in this corpus has had to reach because no earlier ADR was a test.

**A THIRD FAILURE CLASS EXISTS, IT IS REPRODUCED, AND THIS ENTRY DOES NOT REFUSE IT.** [Session 205](sessions/2026-08-25-session-205.md) section 4 found `raw_ingest_rows` declared `derived` through `fills` on the **REVERSE** edge -- `fills.raw_row_id bigint NOT NULL REFERENCES raw_ingest_rows(id)` -- and it **passes both new clauses**: seeded here, with clauses 1 and 2 running, `typecheck` exits 0 and the suite is **green at 113 of 113**. Clause 1 misses it because `raw_ingest_rows` carries no identity column at all, and clause 2 misses it because the column is `NOT NULL`. **A NOT NULL FOREIGN KEY IS NOT A TOTAL RELATION**: `NOT NULL` constrains the child, the traversal needs every PARENT to have a child, and SQL has no declaration for that. **`ledger_transactions` is the registry's only `semi-join` rule and rests on the same unstated property today** -- [`0009_ledger.sql`](../packages/db/migrations/0009_ledger.sql) declares no trigger and no constraint requiring a transaction to have entries. **What separates them is semantic and not syntactic**, so a parser cannot: there the entries ARE the tenancy, and here the row has an owner inside `raw jsonb` that no scope rule reaches. **The ruling therefore covers TWO of the three classes and says so in its own ruling block**, and the remedy it prices is an ATTESTATION on reverse-edge rules -- the exact inverse of clause 3, because a field earns its place exactly when the fact is ABSENT from the primary source. It is not written because it edits `ledgerTransactions`' row.

**THE RULING MET A SLICE NOBODY COORDINATED WITH, AT THE MERGE, AND REFUSED NONE OF IT.** [Session 205](sessions/2026-08-25-session-205.md) merged to `main` while this branch was open, taking the registry from **80 to 87 of 111** and adding **five new `derived` rules** written by an author who had never read [ADR-101](decisions/ADR-101.md): `account_status_history`, `platform_account_refs`, `provisioning_queue`, `platform_entitlements` and `reconciliations`, each hopping `account_id` to `accounts`. **All five satisfy both clauses and not one line of session 205's work was edited.** On the merge result the registry is **87 of 111** at 1 root / 34 owned / 19 derived / 33 firm, **clause 1 refuses 0 of 19, clause 2 refuses 0 of 19, clause 3 passes 34 of 34**, and all three seeds were re-run and are still refused by the same clauses. **The base figures above are left standing rather than rewritten**, because a count is a fact about a tree at a commit and this session's was `fe05a2e`. **The conflict was in [STATE](STATE.md) and [sessions/README](sessions/README.md) only, both appended sections, both keep-both**; the three code files auto-merged, because this session appends 220 lines to the end of one test file and touches no table's rows.

**The position:** `pnpm run typecheck` exit 0 with **zero `error TS`**; `eslint packages/db` exit 0; [`scoped-db.test.ts`](../packages/db/test/scoped-db.test.ts) **101 to 106** at this session's base and **108 to 113** merged; full suite **1,611 to 1,616** at base and **1,618 to 1,623 passed / 1 skipped** merged, over 106 files; `pnpm run gates` 30 of 30; `pnpm run verify` exit 0 at 8 of 8 invariants. **No rule was re-argued and no table's rows were touched.** **One failure class of three remains unrefused and one registered money-path rule rests on it**: the estate is strictly better than before this entry and is not safe, and those are two different statements.

## Session 207: M09's, M11's and M16's tables, and a version table and its acceptances taking DIFFERENT classes on purpose

**FOUR OF FOUR, and the honest form of that number is that nothing was already taken.** `origin/main` was at `4fa5b33` when this branch opened and at `4fa5b33` when it committed, `TABLE_KEYS` at **80** at both reads, so no sibling of the wave merged into the pair while this slice ran and the slice computed is the slice finished. **The registry goes to 84 of 111**, at **1 root, 35 owned, 14 derived and 34 firm**, so **50 of the 84 are reachable through the scoped accessor**. Every figure was recomputed from `TABLE_KEYS.length` rather than incremented.

| Table                       | Migration                                                      | Class                                | Reachable |
| --------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------ | --------- |
| `geo_restrictions`          | [`0004`](../packages/db/migrations/0004_catalog.sql)           | `firm`                               | no        |
| `tos_versions`              | [`0004`](../packages/db/migrations/0004_catalog.sql)           | `firm`                               | no        |
| `tos_acceptances`           | [`0004`](../packages/db/migrations/0004_catalog.sql)           | **`owned`**, `identity_id`, NOT NULL | **yes**   |
| `certificate_verifications` | [`0025`](../packages/db/migrations/0025_reserved_sequence.sql) | `firm`                               | no        |

**THE SLICE WAS COMPUTED AND NOT RECEIVED, AND THE ARITHMETIC IS STATED.** Whole-word match of all 111 migration table names against the three plans returns nine hits for [M09](plans/M09-marketing-site.md), nine for [M11](plans/M11-certificates-social-proof.md) and sixteen for [M16](plans/M16-notification-center.md). Subtracting the 80 already registered leaves `geo_restrictions` and `tos_versions` from M09, `certificate_verifications` and `events` from M11, and `tos_acceptances`, `otp_challenges` and `events` from M16. **`events` and `otp_challenges` are two of the seven standing refusals**, whose reasons are already written in [`scope.ts`](../packages/db/src/scope.ts) and in [ADR-094](decisions/ADR-094.md) section 3 respectively, so they were left alone rather than re-argued. **Four remain and all four were registered.** None of the four unreachable tables ADR-092 section 9 names appeared in the derivation, which is the check that the derivation was not mis-taken.

**THE PAIR IS THE POINT: `tos_versions` AND `tos_acceptances` ARE DECLARED IN THE SAME MIGRATION AND THEIR CLASSES DISAGREE, WHICH IS CORRECT RATHER THAN INCONSISTENT.** One records what the FIRM published and the other records what a PERSON did. `tos_versions` has no identity column and no correct one: every identity is shown the same version and the link runs the other way, `tos_acceptances.tos_version_id` naming the version a person accepted, so ownership flows FROM the published document exactly as it does from `plan_versions`. `tos_acceptances` carries `identity_id uuid NOT NULL REFERENCES identities(id) ON DELETE RESTRICT` on the row and there is no way to write an unowned acceptance. **A shared class would fail in one direction or the other**: firm for both hands nobody their own signature and makes the acceptance record unreadable by the party who made it, and owned for both hides a public legal document behind an identity it does not have.

**AND THE PAIR CARRIES THE FILE'S NAMED TRAP IN ITS MOST PLAUSIBLE DRESS.** `tos_acceptances.tos_version_id` is `uuid NOT NULL REFERENCES tos_versions(id)`, single-valued and declared inline: it reads exactly like `daily_marks`' hop to `accounts` and it is not one, because `tos_versions` is FIRM. **`DerivedRule.via` is typed `TableKey` and includes every firm key, so a `derived` rule through it compiles at every call site and throws the first time anybody reads the table.** It was SEEDED and the bounded assertion failed by name: _"tosAcceptances derives through tosAcceptances -> tosVersions, and tosVersions is firm, so a scoped read of it constructs no predicate and throws"_.

**`certificate_verifications` IS `firm` BECAUSE THE HOP TO `certificates` DOES NOT EXIST, AND THAT IS WORTH SAYING BECAUSE `certificates` IS REGISTERED AND WOULD MAKE A PLAUSIBLE `via`.** The table declares **no foreign key at all**. Its column is `code_hash bytea`, a digest of the ATTEMPTED code, and [`0025`](../packages/db/migrations/0025_reserved_sequence.sql) says why in the column's own comment: storing the codes in the clear would make this table a list of valid tokens for anyone who reached it. A hash addresses no row, `unknown` is one of the four results so most attempts resolve to no certificate at all, and a rule cannot be written through a join the schema refuses to declare. **The class would still be wrong if the join existed**: the signal the table carries is the RATE of `unknown` across all verifiers, which is an enumeration campaign in progress (`AS-M11-04`, `FM-M11-04`), and handing a holder the list of who looked their card up would publish the verifiers instead of the certificate.

**[ADR-094](decisions/ADR-094.md)'S FOLD APPLIES NOTHING TO ANY OF THE FOUR, DERIVED RATHER THAN BELIEVED.** All 84 `ALTER TABLE ... ;` statements across the 47 migrations were extracted with the suite's own multiline match and classified by verb: **no statement in the tree names `geo_restrictions`, `tos_versions`, `tos_acceptances` or `certificate_verifications` in any shape**, so all four are among the undrifted and their comparisons are byte-identical to a pre-ADR-094 one. **The drifted-table sentence therefore stays TEN and only its denominator moves**, from _"of the eighty"_ to _"of the eighty-four"_. **That number cannot be raised by a concurrent sibling either**: of the 31 tables unregistered on open, exactly two carry a later column change and both are standing refusals, `otp_challenges` (`ADD COLUMN` and `ALTER COLUMN`) and `trading_calendar` (`ALTER COLUMN`). **This is the sentence wave 2 merged green and wrong, and deriving it is the only thing that catches that.**

**THREE SEEDS WATCHED FAILING BY NAME, EACH RESTORED AND THE SUITE RE-RUN GREEN AFTERWARDS**, because the green suite is not the check and the reading of the DDL is:

| Seeded                                                                        | Result                                                                                                                                                      |
| ----------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `tosAcceptances` declared `derived` through `tosVersions`, the firm-via trap  | **1 failed**, the bounded chain assertion, naming `tosVersions is firm`                                                                                     |
| `user_agent_class` deleted from the `certificate_verifications` transcription | **1 failed**, _"certificate_verifications: the TS column set equals the set as of the LAST migration"_                                                      |
| `geoRestrictions` declared `owned` on `country_code`                          | **1 failed**, the DDL check quoting `country_code char(2) PRIMARY KEY` against the requirement that an owned column be declared `REFERENCES identities(id)` |

### The refusal: `identity_merges` is the fourth member of a class three sessions have already declined to rule

It carries **`surviving_identity_id` AND `merged_identity_id`, both `uuid NOT NULL REFERENCES identities(id) ON DELETE RESTRICT`** ([`0002_identity.sql`](../packages/db/migrations/0002_identity.sql)), **one index on each** (`identity_merges_surviving_idx`, `identity_merges_merged_idx`), and **`identity_merges_distinct CHECK (surviving_identity_id <> merged_identity_id)`**, which guarantees that every row of the table is a statement about **two different people**. `OwnedRule.column` is ONE column and [`scopePredicate`](../packages/db/src/scoped-db.ts) renders one `eq`.

- **Naming the survivor** drops the row from the merged identity, and [`INV-M7-06`](plans/M07-risk-abuse.md) plus `0002`'s own comment keep that identity alive on purpose: _"the pre-merge history is what a dispute about a grandfathered cap is argued from"_, and the dispute is argued about the merged side's `accounts_at_merge`.
- **Naming the merged identity** drops the row from the survivor, whom the grandfathered cap now binds (B4 #17, `GS-046`).
- **`firm` is refused by the suite's own assertion** that no firm table carries a column referencing `identities`, and it would be a lie about a table with two.

**THE ARGUMENT FOR TAKING `surviving_identity_id` IS RECORDED RATHER THAN LEFT FOR THE NEXT SESSION TO RE-DERIVE, BECAUSE IT IS THE STRONGEST ONE ANY OF THE FOUR REFUSALS HAS FACED.** A hard merge **repoints ownership into the surviving `identities` row**, `identities.id` is the hard-merged grain (already the `why` of the `root` rule), and [`users.md`](architecture/data-model/users.md) says _"one identity may own several users only through a merge"_ -- so the merged identity arguably never holds a scoped session and the survivor's column would cover every read that can actually happen. **That is an inference about application behaviour from prose, and the DDL says the opposite twice**: two `NOT NULL` identity columns and an index on each. The second reason is [`events`](../packages/db/migrations/0017_events_and_audit.sql)' second reason arriving as a **COLUMN** rather than as `jsonb`: the `distinct` CHECK guarantees that whichever side is chosen, the row hands the reader **another identity's uuid**, beside `evidence jsonb` written by a detector, which is what `INV-M4-06` forbids the portal to receive. [ADR-092](decisions/ADR-092.md) section 3 names this class as a per-TABLE ruling and takes neither column. **Wanting a number for it was taken as the stop signal, and no ADR was allocated.**

### The fold status of a table beside a refused one was DERIVED, and the answer is that a refusal does not travel

Both `trading_calendar_loads` and `trading_calendar_revisions` are created by [`0032`](../packages/db/migrations/0032_trading_calendar_holidays_coverage_revisions.sql), **the same migration that carries `trading_calendar`'s two `ALTER TABLE ... ALTER COLUMN ... DROP NOT NULL` statements**, which [ADR-094](decisions/ADR-094.md)'s one-member vocabulary REFUSES.

**Replayed here across all 47 migrations with the suite's own multiline `ALTER TABLE ... ;` match rather than a per-line grep: neither table carries an `ALTER TABLE` of ANY shape** -- not `ADD COLUMN`, not `ADD CONSTRAINT`, not a refused verb -- **and each is created exactly once**. So each one's `CREATE TABLE` body **is** its column set as of the last migration, and a neighbour's refusal is a fact about that neighbour's history.

**IT WAS WATCHED RATHER THAN ASSERTED.** `trading_calendar` was seeded into all three files as a `firm` registration: `no later migration changes a column in a shape ADR-094 does not fold` turned **RED with both `ALTER COLUMN` statements quoted back by filename**, while the two sibling tables from the same migration stayed green in the same run. The seed was reverted and `git status --porcelain` reported clean.

### The three rules, and the one that is a shape rather than a column

**`idempotency_keys` is `owned` on a NULLABLE `identity_id`, and it is `ledger_accounts`' shape and NOT `offers`'.** `identity_id uuid NULL REFERENCES identities(id) ON DELETE RESTRICT` is the only column in the body that reaches a person; the rest are a client token, a route, a digest and a stored response. **`offers` has `offers_identity_scope_matches` making its null biconditional and this table has no CHECK of any kind**, so `identity_id IS NULL` means _no identity was recorded_ and never _the firm owns it_ -- which is why the rule is `owned` on the column the DDL declares against `identities(id)` rather than `firm`. **The DDL already treats the two populations separately in its own index**: `idempotency_keys_identity_idx (identity_id)` is declared `WHERE NOT NULL`.

**`trading_calendar_loads` and `trading_calendar_revisions` are both `firm`, and both `actor` columns are the reason it is a reading rather than a default.** Neither table declares an identity or account column. `actor text NOT NULL` on each is a free-text operator string on `0002`'s idiom, written by the loader and by an operator, **neither of which is a `users` row** -- which is the same shape [`scope.ts`](../packages/db/src/scope.ts)'s own header refuses `treasury_balances.recorded_by` for being.

**`dependent_row_count` IS THE COLUMN MOST LIKELY TO BE MISREAD AS TENANCY AND IT IS A COUNT.** It counts rows in [`fills`](architecture/data-model/fills.md), [`daily_marks`](architecture/data-model/daily_marks.md) and [`rule_states`](architecture/data-model/rule_states.md) that depend on the trading day, asserted a second time by [`0033`](../packages/db/migrations/0033_trading_calendar_revision_required.sql)'s trigger under [ADR-045](decisions/ADR-045.md). **Those three tables are each scoped to an identity and this number is not**, because a count across every account is a property of the DAY.

No table was transcribed, no rule was written, no class was argued, no ADR was allocated and no session number was taken.** [Session 207](sessions/2026-08-25-session-207.md)'s four and [session 208](sessions/2026-08-25-session-208.md)'s three were merged onto `main` at `8914c66` in that order, each verified before the next began. Both branches were re-synced onto `4d29b08` and clean against it, so they conflicted only with each other and with [session 206](sessions/2026-08-25-session-206.md)'s five.

|                     | `TABLE_KEYS` | `scoped-db.test.ts` | Remainder |
| ------------------- | ------------ | ------------------- | --------- |
| `main` at `8914c66` | 92           | **118**             | 19        |
| after session 207   | 96           | **122**             | 15        |
| after session 208   | **99**       | **125**             | **12**    |

**+4 then +3, one new per-table drift assertion per newly registered table and NO EIGHTH.** The count moving DOWN is the failure this arithmetic exists to catch, and it does not: the full suite measured **1,675 passed / 1 skipped on `origin/main` in a throwaway worktree** and **1,682 passed / 1 skipped here**, both ends run rather than inherited, moving by exactly seven.

**THE SEVEN TABLE KEYS WERE DISJOINT AND NOTHING COLLIDED**, so nothing rebased out and no session's work was reduced: `geo_restrictions`, `tos_versions`, `tos_acceptances` and `certificate_verifications` from 207, and `idempotency_keys`, `trading_calendar_loads` and `trading_calendar_revisions` from 208.

**EVERY CODE RESOLUTION WAS STRUCTURAL AND NEVER A HUNK-LEVEL KEEP-BOTH.** Every `pgTable` ends on the same `createdAt` / `updatedAt` / `});` tail, so git aligns on lines two unrelated tables merely share and a kept-both hunk splices one table's columns into another's object literal. Each of the three code files was rebuilt from the current tree's copy and the incoming branch's WHOLE declarations re-appended, after proving each branch's diff against the merge base is an append plus the count literals: **144 lines and four header lines in `schema.ts` for 207, 147 and four for 208**, four and three `SCOPE_RULES` entries with their imports and `TABLES` keys, and four and three `SQL_NAME` pairs. Nothing was reordered and no line of another table was touched. **The `analytics_snapshots` hazard was never reached**, because no resolution searched for a closing marker.

**THE SIX SIZE LITERALS WERE RECOMPUTED FROM `TABLE_KEYS.length` AT EACH MERGE AND NEVER INCREMENTED**: `schema.ts`'s spelled header and its `the other NN` remainder, `scope.ts`'s `TABLES` docblock, the suite's test NAME and its two `expect(...).toBe(N)` assertions, and the remainder in the comment above them.

**THE DRIFTED-TABLE SENTENCE STAYS TEN, DERIVED TWICE AND NOT CARRIED.** Replaying every `ALTER TABLE` across all <!--gen:migration_files-->47<!--/gen--> migrations returns **twelve** tables carrying a later column change at 96 and again at 99, of which `otp_challenges` and `trading_calendar` are unregistered, leaving the same TEN registered names. **None of the seven new tables drifts, so only the denominator moved.** Nothing in the suite checks that sentence; it is prose, and [ADR-042](decisions/ADR-042.md) ruled prose is not a control, which is why it was derived rather than adjusted alongside the five literals that are.

### One `STATE` conflict was a REVISION and keep-both would have merged GREEN AND WRONG

**`docs/STATE.md` is append-only and keep-both holds there, except that this conflict was not an append.** Session 208's branch carried a copy of [session 211](sessions/2026-08-25-session-211.md)'s closing position line reading **109 test files, 1,645 passed** on the tree merged through `4fd4a8a`; `main` carries the same sentence, word for word to its closing clause about `P3-g`, **amended and re-measured on `e7d5e1d` to 111 test files, 1,665 passed**. The line sits ABOVE session 208's own `##` heading and is not its content.

**Keeping both would have put two states of one session's line in one document, the superseded one second, with nothing checking either.** `main`'s REVISION was taken and the stale copy dropped, which is the resolution session 208's own branch took once already at `01e2cd7`. **Session 208's section itself is carried through untouched, as is every other merged session's.**

**The keyed CLAIM table in [`sessions/README`](sessions/README.md) took the opposite resolution, as it always does**: each side struck its own row, so keep-both would answer _has 207 been written_ with yes and no at once. **Unioned by key, taking the STRUCK row** for 206, 207 and 208, no row's text edited. The generated entry span kept all three keys in numeric order, and `gates.mjs generate` reports **every span already matches its query** on the resolved tree, which is what separates a plausible keep-both from one that agrees with its generator.

**THE BRIEF'S ARITHMETIC WAS CHECKED AND IT DOES NOT ADD UP AS WRITTEN, SO WHAT IS ON THE TREE IS REPORTED INSTEAD.** Derived from the migrations: **111 `CREATE TABLE` statements, 99 registered, remainder 12**, and the twelve are

**All five run green on the merge result, and one of them covers a rule this integration carried in.** `idempotency_keys` is `owned` on `identity_id` declaring `nullable: true`, against `identity_id uuid NULL REFERENCES identities(id)` with `idempotency_keys_identity_idx` declared `WHERE NOT NULL` -- so clause 3, the flag checked against the DDL for the first time, agrees with a rule written by an author who had read the entry. `tos_acceptances` is `owned` on a `NOT NULL` column and declares `nullable: false`. **No assertion was weakened and none needed to be.**

### `main` MOVED A THIRD TIME AND IT TOUCHED TWO OF THIS INTEGRATION'S THREE FILES

**`main` went to `c0205ec` while this branch was open, and [#277](https://github.com/lam2-coder/meritfutures/pull/277) is not a transcription: it is the repair for a defect that made EVERY DEPLOYABLE UNABLE TO START.** `tsc` under `moduleResolution: NodeNext` wants `./x.js` for a file that is `x.ts`, while `node --experimental-strip-types` resolves a specifier to the file it names, so **686 relative specifiers were rewritten from `.js` to `.ts`** with `allowImportingTsExtensions` added to `tsconfig.base.json`.

**TWO OF THOSE 686 LINES ARE IN THIS INTEGRATION'S FILES, verified at the source rather than taken on report.** `git diff 8914c66..origin/main` over `packages/db` is exactly two files at one line each: [`scope.ts`](../packages/db/src/scope.ts)'s `./schema.js` becoming `./schema.ts` and [`scoped-db.test.ts`](../packages/db/test/scoped-db.test.ts)'s `../src/index.js` becoming `../src/index.ts`. **[`schema.ts`](../packages/db/src/schema.ts) is untouched by #277.**

**THIS IS THE ONE CASE WHERE THE STRUCTURAL TECHNIQUE IS THE HAZARD RATHER THAN THE REMEDY.** Rebuilding a conflicted file from _a branch's_ copy is exactly how those two lines get reverted, because **both transcription branches predate #277 and still carry the `.js` form**. The technique is right and the phrase _the current tree's copy_ has to mean `main`, never either branch. **It did here by construction**: this branch's two structural rebuilds happened at `8038c89` and `d472c8c`, and the `main` merge that followed **auto-resolved with no conflict at all**, so nothing was rebuilt and both lines landed as `.ts`.

**THE REGRESSION VERIFIES GREEN, SO IT WAS CHECKED BY STARTING A PROCESS.** Vitest resolves either form, so no test in this repository can see it and `pnpm run verify` would have reported success over a tree whose deployables do not run. **Watched instead of asserted**: `apps/api` was started over a real socket under `node --experimental-strip-types` and `GET /api/v1/health` returned **200** with `{"status":"ok"}`; `apps/worker` and `packages/db` were each imported under the same resolver and both load. **The only three relative `.js` specifiers left in the tree are `packages/eslint-plugin-merit/test/*` naming `../index.js`, which IS a real `.js` file**, and all three are byte-identical to `origin/main`.

**The strongest form of the claim is a diff rather than a grep**: `git diff origin/main -- . ':(exclude)packages/db' ':(exclude)docs'` reports **ZERO FILES**, so nothing outside this integration's fence differs from `main` in either direction and no part of #277 was disturbed.

**THE BASELINE WAS RE-MEASURED AGAINST THE NEW `main` RATHER THAN CARRIED.** `c0205ec` in a throwaway worktree gives **111 files, 1,675 passed / 1 skipped** and `scoped-db.test.ts` at **118**, identical to `8914c66` because #277 rewrote import lines and added no test. **So the deltas are unchanged: 118 to 125 and 1,675 to 1,682, +7, one per registered table.**

**The position:** `pnpm run typecheck` exit 0 with **zero `error TS`**; `TABLE_KEYS.length` **99** with 99 `SCOPE_RULES`, 99 `pgTable` declarations and 99 `SQL_NAME` pairs, zero duplicates in any of the three; [`scoped-db.test.ts`](../packages/db/test/scoped-db.test.ts) **125**; `node packages/tooling/checks/repo-invariants.mjs` **8 of 8**; `pnpm run gates` <!--gen:gate_count-->32<!--/gen--> of <!--gen:gate_count-->32<!--/gen-->; `pnpm run verify` **exit 0** at 30 gates clean-and-dirty, **70 scope cases** and 10 loader cases; full suite **111 files, 1,682 passed / 1 skipped** against a measured `origin/main` baseline of **1,675 / 1 skipped**; `lint` and `format:check` clean. **Nothing needed a file outside the fence: no ADR, no migration, no new document, and `docs/plans/**` was read and not edited.**

**THE REGISTRY IS AT ITS CEILING AND THAT IS THE THING WORTH CARRYING FORWARD.** 99 of 111 is not a milestone on the way to 111; **the remaining twelve are unreachable by construction** and every one of them is a per-TABLE ruling nobody has taken or a table no plan names. **The next session that wants a thirteenth needs a ruling and not a transcription.**

**`E2` READ REMAINS PENDING** on the seven money-path registrations these two merges carry in and on the ninety-two before them. **This integration writes no rule and discharges nothing**, and the two merged branches' own claims are carried through as they were written rather than re-verified line by line.

## The accessor learned to WRITE, and the write goes through one door and only inside a transaction (2026-08-25, session 213)

**[ADR-102](decisions/ADR-102.md) lands, `status: proposed`, approval line UNSIGNED, MONEY PATH and the `E2` read owed.** [ADR-008](decisions/ADR-008.md) scoped the accessor to bound a BOLA failure on the READ side and [ADR-084](decisions/ADR-084.md) built it. **Neither ruled on a write, and the write has the same failure mode with worse consequences: a read that returns the wrong rows is a leak, and a row written under the wrong identity is a corruption no later read can tell apart from an honest one.**

**`P3-f` IS THE PRECONDITION UNDER P3's WHOLE WAVE 3 AND TEN SLICES WERE BEHIND IT.** [P3 wave 3](plans/P3-wave3-modules.md) section 6 found that the axis the six modules collide on is the write accessor and not the routes: every one of them writes, and none of them could.

**RULED, in three clauses.** **(1) The write path.** `scopedDb(id)` and `systemDb(reason)` are **UNCHANGED and stay read only**; a write is reached only through `transaction(handle, fn)`. `UPDATE` and `DELETE` carry the same `scopePredicate` the matching read carries, over the whole of `ScopedTableKey`. **An INSERT has no `WHERE` clause, so the identity is WRITTEN**, stamped from the handle, and only `owned` tables have a column to stamp it to: `root` and `derived` inserts are **compile errors**. **The tenancy column is never the caller's to name**, in an insert's values or an update's `SET`, in either spelling. **(2) The transaction.** `SqlExecutor` is the shape [`job-queue.ts`](../packages/queue/src/job-queue.ts)'s `JobTransaction` declares and `transaction()` is its only producer. **(3) The reader with no identity.** `firmDb()` serves `FirmTableKey` and takes **no reason**, and **`SystemReason` stays at two members**.

**NOTHING IN THIS WORKSPACE COULD ENQUEUE A JOB, AND THAT WAS RE-DERIVED AT SOURCE BEFORE IT WAS FIXED.** [`job-queue.ts:162`](../packages/queue/src/job-queue.ts) makes the caller's open transaction `enqueue`'s first argument with no overload that omits it, and [`:59-60`](../packages/queue/src/job-queue.ts) says the type is _"deliberately small enough that `packages/db` can satisfy it without exporting its client"_. **`packages/db` did not satisfy it.** [ADR-006](decisions/ADR-006.md)'s transactional-enqueue criterion has never been gradeable and `P3-l` is the first caller it will be graded against.

**THERE IS NO NON-TRANSACTIONAL WRITE, AND THAT IS `job-queue.ts`'s OWN RULING APPLIED TO THE ACCESSOR RATHER THAN A NEW ONE.** That file's header states it about itself: _"THE AWKWARD ONE TO WRITE IS THE NON-TRANSACTIONAL ONE... There is no `enqueueNow`, no optional transaction and no ambient default."_ A write reachable outside a transaction makes ADR-006's central consequence optional at every call site that forgets it.

**KEEPING THE READ INTERFACES STILL IS A RULING AND NOT A CONVENIENCE, AND IT IS THE MOST USEFUL THING THIS SESSION FOUND.** `CI-01/scope-system-db-not-assignable` seeds a value carrying exactly `__brand`, `reason`, `identityId` and `rows()` and demands the needle `__brand`, on [`falsify-ci.mjs:689-694`](../scripts/ci/falsify-ci.mjs)'s own stated reason that without `identityId` the compiler reports a missing property, _"which passes a naive needle while proving the WRONG THING"_. **A required method added to `ScopedDb` makes TypeScript report four missing properties instead and the case stops proving the brand.** [`falsify-ci.mjs`](../scripts/ci/falsify-ci.mjs) is **outside this session's fence**, so the constraint was met by design rather than by widening: `node scripts/ci/falsify-ci.mjs CI-01` reports **12 of 12**, unchanged, found on `ScopedTableKey` and on `__brand`. **The suite carries a regression guard for the shape, in the package that owns it.**

**A FOURTH FAILURE CLASS EXISTS ON THE WRITE SIDE AND IT IS THE ONLY ONE THIS ENTRY INVENTS A CONTROL FOR. RE-PARENTING.** The predicate matched the row as it stood; a `SET` that moves the tenancy column hands the row to somebody else **after** the predicate agreed to it. **It is least visible on `derived`, where the column being moved is a foreign key and looks like data**: `ledger_entries.ledger_account_id` re-pointed at another identity's ledger account leaves this identity's scope and enters theirs with every check in the package green. `tenancyColumn(key)` returns `rule.localColumn` for `derived`, and the guard refuses both the SQL and the Drizzle spelling.

**OF [ADR-101](decisions/ADR-101.md)'s THREE READ-SIDE FAILURE CLASSES, THE WRITE PATH CANNOT SUFFER ONE, INHERITS ONE HARMLESSLY, AND INHERITS ONE IN THE DIRECTION THAT DESTROYS.** Class 1 cannot arise because the write path never chooses a predicate. Class 2 makes a write touch **fewer** rows than it should, which is a failed write rather than a wrong one. **Class 3 is worse here than on the read side**: a `semi-join` on a non-total reverse edge returns a subset on a read and **deletes a subset and leaves the rest** on a write, with no error anywhere, and `ledger_transactions` is the registry's only `semi-join` rule. **This entry does not close it and it is named rather than glossed.**

**THE THIRD DOOR EXISTS BECAUSE ONE DOOR WAS SERVING TWO DIFFERENT ACTS.** `systemDb(reason).rows(key)` is generic over `TableKey`, so it serves _"EVERYBODY's rows read without their identity"_ -- which is what `'nightly-batch'` and `'operator-console'` do -- **and also "NOBODY's rows"**, which is what reading `coupons` is. **Only the first has an identity at risk.** [ADR-096](decisions/ADR-096.md) is the precedent and **it went the other way**, refusing a third `SystemReason` for `apps/site` on the ground that the site is _"not a reader of this database at all"_; that remedy is unavailable here because under the same entry **`apps/api` is the process the site reads THROUGH**. A third member is refused on ADR-096's own argument -- a list whose third member is _"every request handler"_ is a list nobody has to justify joining -- **and on a second finding it did not have: the reason names the caller and the KEY TYPE names the reach, and they are not connected**, so `systemDb('request-handler')` would have read `accounts` and `payout_requests` firm-wide.

**WHAT THE THIRD DOOR COSTS IS STATED AGAINST THE ENTRY RATHER THAN AROUND IT.** The `firm` classification now decides read and write authorization for **35 tables with no word written at the call site**, and [ADR-101](decisions/ADR-101.md) section 8 records a live blind spot in the only thing that checks it: `no firm table carries a column referencing identities` reads the `CREATE TABLE` and misses `admin_actions.on_behalf_of_identity_id`, `ALTER`-added in [`0043`](../packages/db/migrations/0043_admin_attributed_actions.sql). **It also makes [ADR-096](decisions/ADR-096.md) section 9's measured hole cheaper to fall into**: a site that linked `@merit/db` could previously reach a `firm` table only by writing `systemDb('operator-console')` on a marketing page and can now write `firmDb()`. **`RI-08` is still unwritten and is worth more after this entry than before it.**

**FOUR COMPILE-TIME REFUSALS WERE WATCHED FAILING AND NONE IS PERMANENTLY WATCHED.** A scoped key through `firmDb` (`TS2345` on `FirmTableKey`), a `derived` key through the scoped insert (`TS2345` on `OwnedTableKey`), `root` through the same (`TS2345`), and a `SystemTx` assigned to a `ScopedTx` **with `identityId` present so the BRAND is what refuses** (`TS2322` on `__brand`). **`falsify-ci.mjs` is where they belong and it is outside this fence**, so the follow-on is four case objects taking `CI-01` from 12 to 16, named rather than reached for.

**THREE MUTATIONS WERE WATCHED AND THE THIRD IS THE ONE THAT MATTERS.** Dropping the `WHERE` from the scoped `UPDATE` and `DELETE` fails **5 of 32**; short-circuiting the tenancy guard fails **3**; **making `tenancyColumn` read nothing fails 6**, because a guard that finds nothing looks exactly like a guard with nothing to find, which is [ADR-101](decisions/ADR-101.md)'s own lesson applied before it cost anything. **One weakness in those results is recorded rather than rounded up**: under the third mutation one of the three refusal tests still passes, because the accessor throws a different error whose message the assertion's pattern also matches.

**NOTHING EXECUTED A WRITE AND THE SUITE SAYS SO IN ITS OWN HEADER.** `ci.yml`'s `integration` job runs on bare `ubuntu-latest` with no services block, so there is no Postgres in CI. Every assertion reads the SQL the accessor **builds**, over a driverless Drizzle handle that records what it is asked to run, **so what is asserted is what `scopedTx(...).update(...)` actually sends rather than a reimplementation of it**. **No SUITE in this estate asserts the round trip through a real database, and that is a gap rather than a decision.**

**BUT THE ROUND TRIP WAS EXECUTED BY HAND, ONCE, AND THAT IS THE FIRST TIME THIS CORPUS HAS WATCHED A WRITE BE REFUSED BY A DATABASE RATHER THAN BY AN ASSERTION.** PostgreSQL 16 is available in this container; all **47 migrations applied in order** under `ON_ERROR_STOP=1` giving **112 tables**, and the accessor was driven against it by a scratch script that is **NOT COMMITTED**, because `ci.yml` has no services block and a committed suite that cannot run in CI reports nothing. Eight cases on `wallet_dormancy` with two identities: a scoped read returns **A's row alone**; a scoped `UPDATE` changes **A's row and no other**; **a caller naming its own tenancy column is REFUSED and the transaction ROLLS BACK, the table byte-identical afterwards**; a scoped `DELETE` removes A's row and **leaves B's standing**; a scoped `INSERT` naming no identity lands **owned by A**; a throw after a successful write **rolls it back**; **`tx.sqlExecutor('job-enqueue')` writes on the transaction's own connection and the rollback takes the job with the state change**, which is [ADR-006](decisions/ADR-006.md)'s central consequence executed rather than argued and the first time anything has satisfied `packages/queue`'s `enqueue` contract; and `firmDb().rows('coupons')` is served with no reason written. **It is one run, by hand, of eight cases, on one table, by the session that wrote the code: evidence and not a control.** The remedy is a real `*.integration.test.ts` behind a services block in `ci.yml`, **both outside this fence**.

**THE NEW MODULE WAS LOADED RATHER THAN ASSUMED, AND NO GATE IN THIS ESTATE CHECKS THAT.** [PR #277](https://github.com/lam2-coder/meritfutures/pull/277) established that a `./x.js` specifier type-checks, passes every gate and **cannot be loaded** by the runtime [ADR-083](decisions/ADR-083.md) rules every deployable runs under. `node --experimental-strip-types -e "import('./packages/db/src/index.ts')"` **loads**, and `firmDb`, `transaction` and `tenancyColumn` are in the exported names, so the three things this entry adds are reachable from a running process and not only from `tsc`.

**NO TABLE'S ROWS ARE TOUCHED.** [`scope.ts`](../packages/db/src/scope.ts), [`schema.ts`](../packages/db/src/schema.ts) and [`scoped-db.test.ts`](../packages/db/test/scoped-db.test.ts) are **not edited at all**, which is the whole reason this session ran concurrently with five others, and no table is registered, unregistered or re-argued. **The registry stands at 92 of 111** (1 root / 37 owned / 19 derived / 35 firm) and this session did not move it.

**A BASELINE FIGURE IN THE DISPATCH WAS TEN STALE AND IS REPORTED RATHER THAN INHERITED.** The dispatch named the full suite at **1,665 passed**; measured on this branch's base it is **1,675 passed / 1 skipped** over 111 files.

**THE BASE MOVED WHILE THIS BRANCH WAS OPEN AND EVERYTHING WAS RE-RUN ON THE MERGE RESULT.** [PR #277](https://github.com/lam2-coder/meritfutures/pull/277) merged at `c0205ec`: [session 209](sessions/2026-08-25-session-209.md)'s reported defect repaired, renaming **every relative specifier in the workspace from `.js` to `.ts`** across 178 files, because `node --experimental-strip-types` does not map one onto the other and no deployable in this estate had ever started. **It touched [`scoped-db.ts`](../packages/db/src/scoped-db.ts), [`index.ts`](../packages/db/src/index.ts), [`client.ts`](../packages/db/src/client.ts), [`scope.ts`](../packages/db/src/scope.ts) and [`scoped-db.test.ts`](../packages/db/test/scoped-db.test.ts).** **The conflict was ONE HUNK, in `scoped-db.ts`'s import block, and it was a keep-both**: this session had added `schema.ts` and `FirmTableKey` to the same statements the sweep re-spelled. Nothing else conflicted, because this session appends to the end of one source file and touches no table's rows. **One claim was RE-MEASURED rather than carried**: `admin_actions` is still the only one of the **35** firm tables reaching `identities` directly, folded over all 47 migrations, where [ADR-101](decisions/ADR-101.md) measured it over 31.

**THE BASE MOVED A SECOND TIME AND THE FENCE WAS TESTED BY IT.** [PR #278](https://github.com/lam2-coder/meritfutures/pull/278) merged at `888a4e7`, landing sessions 207 and 208 and taking the registry from **92 to 99 of 111** at **1 root / 39 owned / 19 derived / 40 firm**, which that merge calls the registry's ceiling. **[`scope.ts`](../packages/db/src/scope.ts), [`schema.ts`](../packages/db/src/schema.ts) and [`scoped-db.test.ts`](../packages/db/test/scoped-db.test.ts) auto-merged with NO conflict at all, because this session does not edit them**, and the only conflict was this file, keep-both with the other side first. **THE RULING MET SEVEN TABLES NOBODY COORDINATED WITH AND REFUSED NONE OF THEM**: `write-accessor.test.ts` is **32 passed unchanged**, because every assertion loops over `TABLE_KEYS` rather than over a roster, so the two new `owned` tables are stamped and the five new `firm` tables are served by `firmDb()` with nothing edited. **All three mutations were re-run on the merge result and all three still fail the same assertions** (5, 3 and 6 of 32); `CI-01` **12 of 12**; `packages/db` **9 files / 285 passed**; full suite **112 files / 1,714 passed / 1 skipped**; invariants **8 of 8**; gates **30 of 30**; `verify` exit 0. **`admin_actions` is still the only firm table reaching `identities` directly, now folded over 40 rather than 35.** **The base figures below are left standing rather than rewritten.**

**The position:** `pnpm run typecheck` exit 0 with **zero `error TS`**; `eslint packages/db` exit 0; `write-accessor.test.ts` **32 passed**, a new file that shares none with [`scoped-db.test.ts`](../packages/db/test/scoped-db.test.ts); full suite **111 files / 1,675 passed** to **112 files / 1,707 passed / 1 skipped**; `node packages/tooling/checks/repo-invariants.mjs` **8 of 8**; `pnpm run gates` **30 of 30**; `pnpm run verify` exit 0; `node scripts/ci/falsify-ci.mjs CI-01` **12 of 12**. **Ten slices can start, and the estate is strictly better than before this entry and is not safe.**
