## Column TYPE and NULLABILITY are compared at last, `ALTER COLUMN` stops being a proxy refusal, and the comparison finds nothing (2026-08-25, session 214)

**[ADR-103](decisions/ADR-103.md) lands, `status: proposed`, approval line UNSIGNED, MONEY PATH and the `E2` read owed.** It writes the comparison [ADR-094](decisions/ADR-094.md) section 3 specified, priced as its own session, and did not number.

**THE GAP EVERY SESSION FOR TWO DAYS HAD TO DISCLAIM.** [ADR-084](decisions/ADR-084.md) compares a table's column NAMES against the DDL and [ADR-094](decisions/ADR-094.md) made that comparison read the table's whole history. **The name set was all either of them read.** A column transcribed `text()` where the DDL says `bytea`, or `.notNull()` where the DDL says nullable, agreed on names and was green on all 99 registered tables. **`bytea` versus `text` is [ADR-046](decisions/ADR-046.md)'s seal: `contact_channels.value_hash` is a digest and `value_ciphertext` is envelope-encrypted under a key not present in this database. Money is integer cents, so a wrong integer width is a wrong balance.**

**THE COMPARISON FINDS ZERO DISAGREEMENTS, AND THAT IS THE OPPOSITE OF THE RESULT THE SLICE WAS PRICED FOR.** [P3 wave 3](plans/P3-wave3-modules.md) section 12 row 1 calls its cost _"unmeasured by construction"_, ADR-094 predicted it _"would turn the suite red on whatever it finds"_, and the plan's prompt instructed the session to report rather than repair if the count stopped being small. **Nine sessions transcribed 99 tables and 1,183 columns with nothing checking this axis and got every one of them right.** No row of [`schema.ts`](../packages/db/src/schema.ts) is edited and the file is untouched.

**A GREEN RESULT FROM A NEW COMPARISON IS THE ONE MOST LIKELY TO BE VACUOUS.** Both sides of the per-table assertion are READERS, and two readers that degrade together agree, which is [ADR-084](decisions/ADR-084.md) section 7's failure and [ADR-094](decisions/ADR-094.md)'s seed B. Three assertions stand there: **fourteen sentinel columns written out as LITERALS** and checked against both readers, a non-degeneracy assertion over all 1,183 columns, and an output-vocabulary assertion over sixteen spellings. **Seed B was written for this comparison and watched: with the per-table assertion made to compare the DDL WITH ITSELF and `value_hash` still seeded as `text`, all 99 per-table comparisons stayed GREEN and the sentinel assertion was the only red.**

**`ALTER COLUMN` STOPS BEING A PROXY REFUSAL, AND THE ORDER IS THE RULING.** ADR-094 refused it because _"deleting the refusal before writing the comparison would be trading a real control for nothing"_, so the comparison landed FIRST, in its own commit, watched failing on four seeded transcriptions, and the fold widened after it. **The vocabulary is now two members with the same default of FAIL**, and the `ALTER COLUMN` sub-vocabulary is itself closed at `DROP NOT NULL`: `SET DATA TYPE`, `SET NOT NULL` and both `DEFAULT` shapes have zero instances in 47 migrations and a rule for them would be written against nothing.

**`otp_challenges` AND `trading_calendar` BECOME REGISTRABLE AND NEITHER IS REGISTERED HERE.** Session 215 is unblocked on the first, which is the auth path: `POST /auth/otp` is the only endpoint in the contract that runs before an identity exists.

**THE HONEST COVERAGE IS TWO AXES AND THE ENTRY CARRIES A TABLE OF WHAT IT CANNOT SEE**: `DEFAULT` (335 transcribed calls, and the cheapest next comparison because [ADR-102](decisions/ADR-102.md)'s `insert` already builds statements from it), `CHECK`, `UNIQUE` and indexes, inline `REFERENCES` beyond the columns a scope rule names, and column order. **One fence call is reported rather than taken**: [`schema.ts`](../packages/db/src/schema.ts)'s header now states that `ALTER COLUMN` stays an offender, which is false about this tree; `P3-g`'s fence admits that file for only the rows the comparison finds wrong, the comparison found none, and session 215 holds it next.

**Registry unmoved at 99 of 111.** `scoped-db.test.ts` **125 to 229**, suite **112 files / 1,718** to **112 files / 1,822 passed / 1 skipped**, invariants 9 of 9, gates 30 of 30, `pnpm run verify` exit 0.

## The ledger can be posted to, the imbalance is unrepresentable, and a halt is enforced for the first time since 0016 created it (2026-08-25, session 216)

**[ADR-104](decisions/ADR-104.md) lands, `status: proposed`, approval line UNSIGNED, MONEY PATH and it is the money path's CENTRE: every other money content in P3 posts through it, and the `E2` line-by-line read is owed on every line.** [`packages/ledger`](../packages/ledger/src/index.ts) exists: double-entry posting as a library both `apps/api` and `apps/worker` call, plus `PT-03`'s aggregate half. `ledger_halts` enters the registry and takes it to **100 of 111**.

**THE IMBALANCE IS UNREPRESENTABLE AND NOT MERELY REFUSED, WHICH IS THE ENTRY.** An entry is never constructed. A `Transfer` is, and `entriesOf` emits `+a` against the debit and `-a` against the credit and nothing else in the package emits an entry at all, so the legs of any posting sum to zero **arithmetically** rather than by assertion. **That holds for a `Posting` assembled past both brands by a cast**, because the cast still goes through the same fold, and the suite proves it over the worst forgery the file can write.

**AND THE GUARD IS KEPT, WITH WHAT IT ACTUALLY PROTECTS AGAINST STATED HONESTLY.** `assertBalanced` runs immediately before the first `INSERT` and is **unreachable through `entriesOf` by construction**, so it is not protecting against a caller: it protects against a **later session changing `entriesOf`** -- a third leg shape, a netted amount, an adjustment with no counter-leg -- which every type still compiles through. It is watched refusing a credit that has no debit, driven directly, and the mutation that reaches it end to end is reported rather than committed because a committed test for it would have to break `entriesOf` to exist.

**IT IS A PACKAGE AND THE REASON IS `RI-04` PLUS FOUR NAMED CALLERS ACROSS TWO DEPLOYABLES**: M03's `INV-M3-10` chargeback reversal, M05's `DEP-M3-06`, M08 section 3.1's commission clock and the nightly batch. `packages/ledger` **declares no dependency**, cannot import a client, cannot import `drizzle-orm` or `pg` under `VG-4`, and therefore **cannot open a pool even by mistake**: `postTransaction` takes the caller's OPEN transaction as its first argument with no overload that omits it, which is `job-queue.ts`'s ruling and [ADR-102](decisions/ADR-102.md)'s applied a third time and is [ADR-006](decisions/ADR-006.md)'s central consequence made structural. `LedgerTx` restates ADR-102's `SystemTx` and the suite **READS** [`scoped-db.ts`](../packages/db/src/scoped-db.ts) to bind the two, which is ADR-102's own instrument pointed at `packages/db`.

**THE POSTING PATH DOES NOT RE-IMPLEMENT WHAT THE DATABASE ENFORCES, AND WHICH IS WHOSE IS PARTITIONED LINE BY LINE.** Seven invariants are the schema's and are relied on rather than restated (`INV-M5-04`'s deferred zero-sum trigger, `LEDGER-C1`, `LEDGER-C2`, `amount_cents <> 0`, the uniques, the reversal constraint, both foreign keys). Seven are this path's and **not one of them is checkable by the database as it stands**: balance before the write, `LEDGER-C1` at three scales including over the RESOLVED uuids, a positive transfer amount, `bigint` cents at runtime, the halt, the empty transaction, and the code-to-scope partition.

**A LIVE `ledger_halts` ROW REFUSES THE POSTING, AND THE FINDING IS THAT NOTHING HAS EVER ENFORCED THAT TABLE.** `grep -n TRIGGER` over [`0016_treasury_controls.sql`](../packages/db/migrations/0016_treasury_controls.sql) returns **zero**, and the table's own escalation index calls itself _"the read every payout and withdrawal path makes before it moves money for this identity"_ -- a read, made by a code path, and until this entry **no code path made it**. The check is INSIDE `postTransaction` rather than beside it, because a control a caller is asked to remember is the shape ADR-008 and ADR-102 both reject. The override is a WORD from a closed one-member vocabulary, `'halt-remediation'`, on `sqlExecutor`'s precedent, because releasing a halt often requires posting a correction and a halt that refused its own remediation is a halt somebody turns off.

**A FINDING THIS SESSION DID NOT EXPECT, AND IT WAS EXECUTED RATHER THAN ARGUED.** `ledger_entries_zero_sum` is `AFTER INSERT ON ledger_entries`, so **a `ledger_transactions` row with NO ENTRIES fires it zero times and commits clean**. That is [ADR-101](decisions/ADR-101.md) section 7's open failure class with a **producer** rather than a hypothesis: the property that entry says SQL "has no way to declare" is falsifiable by one ordinary `INSERT`. `posting()` refuses the shape and the database does not. **The remedy is a deferred constraint trigger, which is a migration, and [P3 wave 3](plans/P3-wave3-modules.md) says no wave-3 slice is dispatched with one -- so `0048` STAYS FREE and the finding is reported instead of taken.**

**OF ADR-101's FOUR FAILURE CLASSES, THREE CANNOT ARISE ON THIS PATH AND THE FOURTH IS INHERITED AS THE POPULATION RATHER THAN AS THE STATEMENT.** This path evaluates no scope predicate at all -- `SystemTx.insert` renders an `INSERT` with no `WHERE` -- and `LedgerTx` names no `UPDATE` and no `DELETE`, so the statement that could return or destroy a subset does not exist here whatever authority the injected handle carries. But **the rows this path writes are exactly the rows the `semi-join` on `ledger_transactions` traverses**, and ADR-102 records that a `DELETE` through that rule deletes a subset and leaves the rest. This entry is the producer of that population and it does not close the class.

**TWO THINGS ADR-102's ACCESSOR DOES NOT OFFER, REPORTED RATHER THAN ROUTED AROUND.**

**THE REASON PROBLEM, AND IT BLOCKS SESSION 220.** A double-entry posting touches two parties' accounts by construction, so no single-identity handle writes it; `firmDb()` cannot either, because both `ledgerTransactions` and `ledgerEntries` are `derived` and `FirmTx.insert` takes `FirmTableKey`. That leaves `SystemTx`, whose vocabulary is exactly `'nightly-batch' | 'operator-console'` -- and **a checkout posting from `apps/api` is neither word**. This is ADR-102 clause 3's read-side gap arriving on the write side, where its own remedy does not reach. **Nothing here is blocked and `P3-n` will be**, so three readings are priced in the entry for the session that must take one, and `accessor-bind.test.ts` **watches the vocabulary** so that a third member closes the finding rather than hiding it.

**THERE IS NO READ THAT CARRIES A PREDICATE.** `rows(key)` renders `SELECT *` with no `WHERE`, so resolving one posting reads the **whole chart of accounts** and the halt check reads **every halt row ever written**. The path does not reach around it: `readChart` is separated from `postTransaction` and returns a value, so the window is the caller's -- a batch reads once and posts thousands. **The cost is stated at the call site** in [`chart.ts`](../packages/ledger/src/chart.ts)'s own header rather than only in the entry, and the remedy is a diff on `packages/db`.

**`PT-03` IS ASSERTED OVER WHAT WAS WRITTEN AND NOT OVER WHAT WAS BUILT.** `0027`'s trigger reads one `transaction_id`, so a ledger in which every transaction balances and the whole does not is one it reports as healthy: the aggregate half sums the `ledger_entries` rows the writer was **asked to insert**, so a path dropping a leg between the value and the INSERT fails and a property over `entriesOf` alone would not. The property is watched **not being vacuous** by counting postings, entries and multi-leg postings actually generated. Every generated value is `bigint` from `fc.bigInt`, so no `number` exists on this path at any point. **`GS-231` stays `blocked / no-fixture-format`** and section 39 is untouched.

**SIX MUTATIONS WATCHED, EACH REVERTED AND DIFFED BYTE-FOR-BYTE AGAINST A PRE-SEED COPY.** `entriesOf` dropping the credit leg fails **26 of 57** including the central claim itself; `accountKey` forgetting the identity fails **16**; the `LEDGER-C1` mirror never firing fails **2**; the halt no-op **1**; a negative amount accepted **1**; plus a compile refusal on a firm code passed to `identityAccount`. **TWO OF THE SIX ARE WEAK AND ARE RECORDED RATHER THAN ROUNDED UP.** The `accountKey` seed is the one worth the most, because it merges two traders' positions while leaving every arithmetic property green in isolation, and it is the seed nobody would think to write.

**THE ROUND TRIP WAS EXECUTED, AND TWO OF ITS ELEVEN ROWS ARE A PAIR.** PostgreSQL 16, all 47 migrations under `ON_ERROR_STOP=1`, 111 tables. **A credit with no debit written with the path BYPASSED was REFUSED BY THE DATABASE AT COMMIT**, naming the net in cents -- the approval clause's second half, executed. **The same posting bypassed with a live halt COMMITTED** -- the halt finding, executed. Together they say which control holds which line: an unbalanced write is refused whatever route it takes, and a halted write is refused by nothing at all unless it comes through this library. Aggregate over the real table: **0 cents over 8 entries**. **1** empty transaction left standing on purpose. **The script is not committed** -- `ci.yml` has no services block -- and it is evidence rather than a control, naming the same `*.integration.test.ts` follow-on ADR-102 named, **which is now two consecutive money-path entries asking for it**.

**TWO FILES OUTSIDE THE STATED FENCE, BOTH FORCED, BOTH MEASURED BOTH WAYS, AND BOTH REPORTED IN THE PULL-REQUEST BODY.** [`pnpm-lock.yaml`](../pnpm-lock.yaml): `pnpm install --frozen-lockfile` **refuses** a workspace package whose devDependencies are absent from the lockfile and **passes** if the package declares none, so the fence was keepable at the price of making a money-path package the estate's first phantom-dependency one. The dependencies are declared and the lockfile is REGENERATED rather than hand-edited, **15 lines, one importer block**. **It also refutes the plan's own concurrency claim**: section 6.2 says a library slice collides with nothing, and `pnpm-lock.yaml` is shared with session 217's new package. [`gates.mjs`](../scripts/corpus/gates.mjs), one line: **`CI-06o` failed on the good news at 29 of 30** and named its own remedy -- a money path absent from its scope list is ADR-044 prohibition 1 unenforced over it -- so adding the package brings it UNDER the gate, which is the opposite of weakening one.

**BASELINES WERE RE-DERIVED AT `00326ad` RATHER THAN TRUSTED, AND ALL FIVE MATCHED THE DISPATCH** for the first time in this wave: registry 99 of 111, gates 30 of 30, invariants 9 of 9, suite 112 files / 1,718 passed / 1 skipped, `verify` exit 0.

**THIS ENTRY WAS `ADR-103` AND THE COLLISION WAS THREE-WAY, WHICH MAKES IT THE DISPATCH'S RATHER THAN ANY SESSION'S.** Sessions **214**, **216** and **217** were dispatched concurrently, each read the register correctly, each found `102` as the highest allocated, and each took `103`. Session 214 merged first at `09c2943`, so `ADR-103` is its column-type ruling; this is **`ADR-104`** and session 217 takes `105`, both assigned centrally so the retry cannot collide again. `104` was verified free against `main` **and against all 228 remote refs** before it was taken. **One observation was reported rather than resolved quietly while it stood: `origin/claude/s217-p3m-psp-port` carried an `ADR-104` of its own**, having renumbered itself once before the central assignment reached it. **THAT COLLISION IS NOW CLOSED.** Session 217 landed `7a44da5` -- _"Renumber to ADR-105: the tiebreak said WHO moves and not WHICH number"_ -- renaming its own file and recording `103` against session 214, `104` against this branch and `105` against its own in its `ALLOCATION` table. **Both branches agree on all three numbers and `104` is unambiguously this one.**

**THE RENUMBER'S SCOPE WAS ENUMERATED BY GREP AND EACH OF THE SIXTEEN LINES WAS ATTRIBUTED BEFORE IT MOVED.** After the merge the tree holds BOTH entries' citations in three of the same files -- [`scoped-db.test.ts`](../packages/db/test/scoped-db.test.ts) holds fourteen of session 214's and exactly one of this session's, this file holds one of each, and [ALLOCATION](decisions/ALLOCATION.md) holds one row each -- so a blanket substitution would have renumbered session 214's entry inside its own work. **One of the sixteen was a MISATTRIBUTION rather than a renumber**: [`gates.mjs`](../scripts/corpus/gates.mjs) read _"ADR-103 landed the posting path"_, which is not true of the entry that now holds that number, and it cites `ADR-104` because that is the one that did.

**SESSION 214'S NEW ASSERTION MET `ledger_halts` AND REFUSED NOTHING, WHICH IS WORTH MORE THAN ANY COUNT HERE.** That session added a per-column TYPE and NULLABILITY comparison over every registered table -- the axis [ADR-094](decisions/ADR-094.md) section 3 named as never compared on any table -- and its author had never seen this table. On the merge result `ledger_halts: every column's TYPE and NULLABILITY equal the DDL as of the LAST migration` **passes on all thirteen columns, with not one line of either session's work edited to make it so.**

**RE-DERIVED ON THE MERGE RESULT RATHER THAN CARRIED**: registry **100 of 111** unmoved by the merge, `packages/db` **14 files / 448 passed**, full suite **117 files / 1,881 passed / 1 skipped**, invariants **9 of 9**, gates **30 of 30**, `verify` **exit 0**. **The merge conflicted in five documents and in NO SOURCE FILE**: `schema.ts`, `scope.ts` and `scoped-db.test.ts` all auto-merged, which is the per-table fence tested rather than asserted.

**A LANDMINE CREATED AND CAUGHT IN THIS SESSION, RECORDED SO THE NEXT ONE DOES NOT REPEAT IT.** `scripts/` is **outside** the root `format` script's glob. Running Prettier over [`gates.mjs`](../scripts/corpus/gates.mjs) by hand reformatted **156 lines** of a file whose one-line change is the whole reason for touching it, and `format:check` would not have said so in either direction. Reverted from the index, the one-word correction re-applied, and the diff against `main` is back to 11 insertions and 3 deletions.

**The position:** registry **100 of 111** at 1 root / 40 owned / 19 derived / 40 firm; `packages/ledger` **5 files / 57 passed**; full suite **117 files / 1,776 passed / 1 skipped**; `typecheck` exit 0 with **zero `error TS`**; `eslint .` exit 0; `format:check` clean; invariants **9 of 9**; gates **30 of 30**; `pnpm run verify` **exit 0**; the module LOADED under `node --experimental-strip-types` with 17 exports. No migration, no `CI-06` letter, no gate register row, no `VG` row, no `RI-nn`, no `SD-nn`, no `OI-nn`, no fixture, no edge case, no dependency and therefore no `VG-12` admission, no `build` script, no route and nothing under `apps/`. **NOT MERGED. The `E2` read is owed.**

## `packages/psp` exists: the `PspAdapter` port and two fakes (2026-08-25, session 217)

**[ADR-105](decisions/ADR-105.md) is proposed, `status: proposed`, approval line UNSIGNED, MONEY PATH by subject.** [P3 wave 3](plans/P3-wave3-modules.md)'s `P3-m` slice is written: one package, five methods, two fakes, 69 tests over 4 files. **No route, no network, no vendor SDK, no dependency, no migration and no row written.**

**THE RULING IN ONE LINE IS THAT THE PORT OWNS THE ORDER AND THE ADAPTER OWNS THE MECHANICS.** `verifyHmacWebhook` runs digest, then freshness window, then parse, once, for every provider; an `HmacWebhookScheme` supplies the vendor half. **The parse is inside the verifier and there is no other parse**, so [`API_CONTRACT:629`](architecture/API_CONTRACT.md)'s _"HMAC signature verified before parsing"_ is a module boundary rather than a convention a handler could get wrong.

**Three things this slice found that later slices inherit.**

| #     | Finding                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                   | Who it lands on                                                                                                                                                                                                          |
| ----- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| **1** | **The amount a card is charged is not `amount_paid_cents`.** [`0006_commerce.sql:189`](../packages/db/migrations/0006_commerce.sql)'s `purchases_wallet_leg_matches_method` permits `0 < wallet_debit_cents < amount_paid_cents` on `mixed`, and [ADR-019](decisions/ADR-019.md) admitted `mixed` because _"a trader with $60 in the wallet buying a $99 evaluation is the common case"_. **A port taking a plain `amountCents` would have charged the card 9900 instead of 3900 with every type in the workspace green** | **Session 220**, `POST /checkout`. `cardLegOf` is the only producer of the amount and it refuses a wallet-funded row                                                                                                     |
| **2** | **A signature refusal has a ROW to write, so the throw cannot be bare.** `psp_webhook_events.signature_verified` is `boolean NOT NULL` and `processing_result` carries `'rejected_signature'`, so a catch block needs the provider and the raw bytes                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      | **Session 219**, the webhook receiver. `WebhookVerificationError` carries `psp`, a closed `refusal` and `raw`                                                                                                            |
| **3** | **`packages/psp` is money path by subject and is scanned by nothing for a model-SDK import.** `CI06O_SCOPE` is `['packages/rules-engine']` and `CI-06o`'s discovery half recognises a money path by directory name against `MONEY_PATH_WORDS`, `['rules-engine', 'payout', 'ledger', 'auth']`. **`psp` is in neither.** [Session 157](sessions/2026-08-24-session-157.md)'s `M3-h` fence held `gates.mjs`; this plan's `P3-m` fence does not, and the plan wins                                                           | **Unassigned.** One array element, in a file this fence excludes. **`packages/ledger` (session 216) has the same shape and its word IS in the list**, so that slice will trip the gate where this one is invisible to it |

**Nothing is admitted.** `node:crypto` is a Node builtin, banned only in `packages/rules-engine/src` under `RE-D-03`. [`pnpm-workspace.yaml`](../pnpm-workspace.yaml) is untouched, [`pnpm-lock.yaml`](../pnpm-lock.yaml) is **+12 insertions and 0 deletions** and all of it is this package's own `importers` block, `onlyBuiltDependencies` stays `[]`, and no `build` script exists.

**Measured on this branch, not inherited.** Suite **112 files / 1,718 passed** to **116 files / 1,787 passed / 1 skipped**; `typecheck` exit 0; `eslint packages/psp` exit 0; invariants **9 of 9**; gates **30 of 30**; `verify` exit 0; registry unmoved at **99 of 111**, because this slice touches no `packages/db` file at all. The module **loads under `node --experimental-strip-types` with 21 exports**, which is [PR #277](https://github.com/lam2-coder/meritfutures/pull/277)'s regression class checked rather than assumed.

**`CI-05` REFUSED THIS SLICE'S OWN TEST FILE AND THE GATE WAS RIGHT.** `gitleaks` reported two `generic-api-key` findings at entropy 4.28 on the two fixture secrets, which were a real provider's webhook-secret prefix plus sixteen hex characters: a credential **by shape**. Nothing live was exposed, and _"it was only a fixture"_ is the sentence `VG-1` exists so that nobody has to trust. **Two consequences, and the second outlives this slice.** **(1) `pnpm run verify` is green on a tree `CI-05` refuses**, because [`package.json:16`](../package.json) rules the scanners out of `verify` on a sound stated reason, so **`verify` exit 0 is not sufficient evidence for a session-end claim** and this slice's first pull-request body made exactly that claim. **(2) `gitleaks git .` reads HISTORY** ([`ci.yml:237-241`](../.github/workflows/ci.yml), `fetch-depth: 0`, deliberate), so a forward fix cannot clear it; the branch history was rewritten with founder authorisation, all nine commits replayed with the two literals substituted and every message, author and date preserved. **The remedy that was refused is the one inside the fence**: a `.gitleaks.toml` allowlist is weakening a gate to pass it, and it exempts the PATH permanently where the defect was one STRING once.

**Nine mutations seeded, three survived the first pass, all three closed with a case each.** The one worth carrying is the MAC length guard: `timingSafeEqual` **throws** on a length mismatch rather than returning `false`, so dropping the guard makes the route return **500 where the contract requires 401 and a security event**, and no case in the suite presented a well-formed MAC of the wrong size until one was written.

## A row that belongs to TWO identities is scoped to NEITHER, and the scope vocabulary gains its fifth and last class (2026-08-25, session 215)

**[ADR-106](decisions/ADR-106.md) lands, `status: proposed`, approval line UNSIGNED, MONEY PATH and the `E2` read is owed on it.** The registry goes **100 to 104 of 111**: `identity_links`, `dedupe_matches` and `attributions` enter as `pair`, and `otp_challenges` as `firm`. **Four sessions had reached this class and stopped correctly** -- [session 161](sessions/2026-08-24-session-161.md), [session 162](sessions/2026-08-24-session-162.md), [session 194](sessions/2026-08-25-session-194.md) and [session 208](sessions/2026-08-25-session-208.md) -- and each stopped because a transcription rules nothing. **This one had the number.**

**THE VOCABULARY'S OWN CLAIM TO BE CLOSED AT FOUR WAS FALSE, AND THE COUNTER-EXAMPLE PREDATES IT BY EVERY MIGRATION IN THE TREE.** [`scope.ts`](../packages/db/src/scope.ts) declared _"The question has exactly these four answers on this schema, which is what makes the vocabulary closed rather than merely short"_, and `0002_identity.sql` created `identity_links` with two `NOT NULL REFERENCES identities(id)` columns on the day the schema was written. **Exactly four tables in 111 declare more than one**, measured by reading every `CREATE TABLE` body rather than by trusting a list: `identity_links`, `dedupe_matches`, `attributions` and `identity_merges`.

**THE CLASS DOES NOT MAKE THE TABLES SCOPED-READABLE, AND THAT IS THE RULING RATHER THAN A LIMITATION.** The predicate exists and is one line: `columnA = $1 OR columnB = $1` returns precisely the rows that are one person's and no others. **What it returns is the problem.** Every such row carries the OTHER party's identity uuid out of a `NOT NULL` column, and on both canonical-order tables the database guarantees that column names somebody else. **The corpus had already ruled exactly this at arity three and the ruling is applied rather than invented**: `correlation_groups` is `firm` and its own `why` says _"the reason it MUST NOT be traversed is stronger than the reason it cannot: returning the row to each member would tell every member which OTHER accounts the detector grouped them with"_. At arity two the disclosure is **worse rather than milder** -- a member of a three-account group learns a set, and a party to a two-identity row learns precisely who.

**A SCOPED READ IS A FILTER AND NOT A PROJECTION**, which is the sentence the whole clause rests on. Registering under the disjunction would have handed the projection the entire job of not disclosing the counterparty, which is the position [ADR-008](decisions/ADR-008.md) scoped the accessor to stop relying on.

**THE COUNTER-ARGUMENT IS REAL AND IS ANSWERED RATHER THAN IGNORED.** `risk_flags`, `identity_signals` and `kyc_verifications` are registered and all carry detector or provider material, and `risk_flags`' own `why` says _"REGISTERING A TABLE MAKES IT READABLE AND NOTHING ELSE"_. **That position is right and is not disturbed.** Every one of those tables names exactly ONE person; what a pair row adds is not sensitivity but a SECOND SUBJECT, arriving as the tenancy column itself, so no reader can project it away without projecting away the thing that made the row reachable.

**A `pair` KEY IS THE FIRST `TableKey` THAT IS A MEMBER OF NEITHER NARROW TYPE.** It is excluded from `ScopedTableKey` for the disclosure and from `FirmTableKey` because [ADR-102](decisions/ADR-102.md) clause 5 gives `firmDb()` no reason on the ground that _"no identity is at risk"_, and here two are. **`ScopedTableKey` and `FirmTableKey` no longer partition `TableKey`**, and the suite asserts the three-way split. `systemDb(reason)` is the only door -- which is what [M06](plans/M06-admin-ops-console.md)'s console and [M07](plans/M07-risk-abuse.md)'s detectors, **the only readers of `identity_links` the corpus names**, actually need. **Traders still have none, and `INV-M7-09` is the sentence that looks like a counter-example and is not**: a trader may CONTEST a link and the contested link is visible **to the admin who acts on it**.

**`otp_challenges` IS THE FIRST `firm` ROW WHOSE REASON IS TIMING RATHER THAN OWNERSHIP.** Every other firm table holds a row no identity will EVER own; this one holds a row whose identity does not exist YET, because `POST /auth/otp` is the only endpoint in the contract at required factor `none`. **It is also the first registered table to exercise [ADR-103](decisions/ADR-103.md)'s second fold member**, which closes [session 214](sessions/2026-08-25-session-214.md)'s named landmine: `foldTable(...).relaxed` was empty on all 99 registered tables and the member ran only on two tables the suite folds by name.

## Session 222: the provisioning saga, and an admission nobody can construct without the evidence

**[ADR-107](decisions/ADR-107.md) is proposed, `status: proposed`, approval line UNSIGNED, MONEY PATH, `E2` read owed.** [P3 wave 3](plans/P3-wave3-modules.md)'s `P3-l` slice is written: seven files under [`apps/worker/src/provisioning/`](../apps/worker/src/provisioning/index.ts) and **62 tests**. **No route, no `packages/db` file, no migration, no dependency and no `pnpm-workspace.yaml` change.**

**THE RULING IN ONE LINE IS THAT THE FAIL-CLOSED EXIT IS A VALUE WITH ONE PRODUCER RATHER THAN A CHECK THAT REFUSES.** `SetpointConfirmation` is branded on a module-local `unique symbol`, `setpointConfirmation` is its only producer, and `TradingAdmission`'s admitted arm carries one as a required field. **ADR-006's transactional-enqueue criterion has a caller for the first time.** [`job-queue.ts`](../packages/queue/src/job-queue.ts) has said since [session 147](sessions/2026-08-24-session-147.md) that nothing in this workspace could produce the `JobTransaction` its `enqueue` requires; [ADR-102](decisions/ADR-102.md) produced one and `enqueueProvisioningOp` puts the `provisioning_queue` INSERT and the job on **one** handle. ## `P3-j` has landed: the authentication surface, and the three writes nothing in this repository can express (2026-08-26, session 218)

**Fifteen endpoints across two files, 43 tests, no dependency and no ADR.** [API_CONTRACT](architecture/API_CONTRACT.md) section 3's seven headings, section 3.1's six endpoints and `GET /me` are written in [`apps/api/src/routes/auth.ts`](../apps/api/src/routes/auth.ts) and [`apps/api/src/routes/me.ts`](../apps/api/src/routes/me.ts). All fifteen register on the public surface and **every one of them is withheld from the operator surface**, both directions read out of `buildServer`'s own composition report rather than counted by hand. Merged with `origin/main` the public surface composes **four modules and 17 routes** and the operator surface **1 of 17**: `auth`, `me`, [`health`](../apps/api/src/routes/health.ts) and session 224's [`public-methods`](../apps/api/src/routes/public-methods.ts).

**The plan was committed and pushed before the first source file existed.** [ADR-003](decisions/ADR-003.md) asks for plan mode on a money path; a remote autonomous session that enters the harness's plan mode blocks on an approval prompt nobody is watching, so the discipline is discharged in writing. That commit is the gate and it is the first on the branch.

### `C-27` is a type, and the seed is a compiler directive

`ElevationFactor` admits `passkey` and `dual_channel` and nothing else, which is `sessions.elevated_by_factor`'s CHECK list at `0029:581` written as a union. So an SMS-offered elevation is **not a value of `ElevateRequest`**, which is section 12's *"there is no such value to send"* made true rather than restated.

**Both directions of that claim were executed rather than asserted.** A seeded handler comparing the parsed factor against `sms_otp` is **`TS2367`**, *"types `"passkey" | "dual_channel"` and `"sms_otp"` have no overlap"*; and widening the union turns all three `@ts-expect-error` directives in the suite into **`TS2578`** unused-directive errors. `apps/api/tsconfig.json` includes `test/**/*.ts`, so the refusal is checked by `pnpm run typecheck` and not by a test somebody could delete.

### The required factor is declared once per endpoint and it is load bearing

The route list and the declaration table are **derived from the same array**, so a route cannot be registered without stating its factor and the two cannot drift. `endpointHandler` applies the declared factor before any handler body runs, and **no handler in either file contains an authorization check of its own**. Section 12's second assertion is asserted as a biconditional: a `C-27:` tag and a non-single factor are the same rows, in both directions.

**`RouteDefinition` has nowhere to put this**, so it lives in a module-level export. A later gate that reads declarations out of the code rather than out of the document has to know that, and every route slice behind this one will place it somewhere of its own choosing unless [ADR-100](decisions/ADR-100.md)'s registry grows the field.

### Section 12's six rows, in both directions, and ten mutations

The two quiet rows are the ones worth naming: `GET /sessions` and `GET /phone/change` return **200** from a single-factor session, and the read that showed the destination is watched succeeding **from the same session** whose write is refused, because two tests using two sessions would not show it is the same caller.

**Ten mutations were seeded one at a time and every one was caught** at 4, 2, 2, 3, 5, 5, 3, 1, 1 and 1 failures: the two `C-27` rows losing their factor, the two quiet rows gaining one, `authorize` ceasing to read elevation, `authorize` answering 403 to an anonymous caller, the 403 ceasing to name the factor, `Retry-After` dropped, the degraded 202 losing `deferred`, and `GET /me` becoming a pass-through. Every seed was removed with `git status --porcelain` empty.

**No number in either file is a rate limit.** Both the SMS and the EMAIL branch go through one port method, and the suite drives the velocity by counting to a `send_limit` read off a seeded `otp_send_budget` row, so the limit is data in the test as well as in the handler.

### The finding: three writes, and nothing in this repository can express any of them

| Write | Why |
|---|---|
| revoke ONE session | `ScopedTx.update` renders `scopePredicate(key, identityId)` and **takes no second predicate**, so it writes every session that identity holds |
| consume ONE otp challenge | `otp_challenges` is `firm`, so `scopedTx` refuses it at compile time and the firm door is the defect below |
| stamp `elevated_at` on ONE session | as the first |

`systemTx.update` ([`scoped-db.ts:701`](../packages/db/src/scoped-db.ts)) and `firmTx.update` (`:720`) render **no `WHERE` clause at all**, which is [session 222](sessions/2026-08-26-session-222.md)'s finding, confirmed from the API side. **What is new here is `scopedTx.update`**, which looks like the safe door and is not: its blast radius is one trader logged out of every device instead of one, with every type in the workspace green, and that is the size that survives review.

**And the remedy the dispatch offered is not available.** `SqlExecutorReason` is closed at `'job-enqueue'` ([`scoped-db.ts:567`](../packages/db/src/scoped-db.ts)) and `sqlExecutorOn` throws on any other word, so reaching raw SQL from a route handler means editing that file. So `AuthBackend` is **declared and blocked on its own declaration**, its default throws on all sixteen methods, and every route answers **503 `service_unavailable`** until a store is wired. Nothing is routed around.

**Three of the dispatch's six cited line numbers do not resolve**: `systemTx.rows` is 695, `firmTx.update` is 720 and `firmTx.delete` is 723, not 694, 718 and 721. The defect is entirely real and what drifted is the coordinate, which is why the header in [`auth.ts`](../apps/api/src/routes/auth.ts) names the method first and the line second.

### Two things recorded rather than ruled

| # | Item | Disposition |
|---|---|---|
| **1** | **`POST /phone/change/:id/cancel` has no required factor anywhere in the corpus.** Section 3.1 declares one for opening a change and one for reading one and says nothing about cancelling | Declared `session` on the contract's **own** argument, that requiring elevation to STOP an attacker's ceremony would lock the real owner out of the control that helps them. **A debt against section 12**, which is outside this fence |
| **2** | **`POST /auth/elevate`'s declared cell reads `session` where section 12's reads `passkey or dual_channel`** | Not an error. That cell names the factor the **elevation admits**; section 3 says *"Auth: session"* and *"it never issues a new one"*, so a caller with no session has nothing to elevate. `CI-06k` reads the document and never this array |

**A third is a contradiction inside API_CONTRACT itself and it is reported, not resolved.** Section 3 says *"the response is unchanged and `deferred` is set"* and, one sentence later, that distinguishing the degraded response *"would tell an attacker exactly when their own traffic tripped the breaker"*. A response carrying `deferred` **is** distinguishable, and `OtpResponse202` declares the field. The declared type is implemented and the status-is-unchanged reading is taken; the resolution is a ruling on a frozen document.

### `ADR-108`'s row is NOT deleted, and the gate is the reason

The disposition [ADR-034](decisions/ADR-034.md) requires of an unused reservation is deletion, and it was asked for here in the same breath as `ADR-111`'s, which was deleted on `main` at `d2e12c5`. **It is not executable for `108`, and the difference is arithmetic rather than judgement.** `111` was the HIGHEST claimed number, so removing it left the range intact; `108` sits under `109`, still reserved for session 219, and under `110`, now `accepted`. Deleting it was attempted and `CI-06f` refused it by name:

```
FAIL   CI-06f  ADR numbers are unique and gapless over allocated plus reserved  (1)
       ADR-108 is neither present nor reserved (a hole)
```

which is [ALLOCATION](decisions/ALLOCATION.md)'s own warning that *"a vacated number reserves nothing and an early renumber fails the gate"*, met head on. **The row is restored and left exactly as dispatched.** It becomes deletable when nothing claims a number above it, which is a compaction somebody performs deliberately once session 219's `109` resolves, and never a side effect of this branch landing. Never weaken a gate to pass it.

**A third instance of the coordinate drift this session already reported.** The dispatch that independently confirmed the `scopedTx` finding cited `scoped-db.ts:566`, `:741` and `:671`; against a `scoped-db.ts` byte-identical to `main`'s they are **`:567`, `:742` and `:676`**. This session's own three, `:567`, `:701` and `:720`, were re-run on the merged tree and all three resolve. **The defect is exact every time and the coordinate is wrong most times**, which is the argument for naming the METHOD before the line, and `:676` is now pinned in [`auth.ts`](../apps/api/src/routes/auth.ts)'s header for the `scopedTx.update` row.

### Nothing is admitted, and no number is reserved

[`pnpm-workspace.yaml`](../pnpm-workspace.yaml), [`pnpm-lock.yaml`](../pnpm-lock.yaml) and [`apps/api/package.json`](../apps/api/package.json) are **all untouched**, which the fence permitted and the work did not need: a WebAuthn verifier admitted here would sit behind a port that throws, because a passkey assertion cannot be verified without the credential store and `passkeys` lives in `packages/db`. The lockfile is rowed **SERIAL** across `P3-j`, `P3-m` and `P4-i`, so not taking it is a scheduling result and not only a tidiness one. **`ADR-108`'s conditional reservation stands exactly as dispatched** and is deleted by whoever lands next.

Merged with sessions 224 and 225 the tree reads **126 files / 2,119 passed / 1 skipped**, `apps/api` at **6 / 94**, measured after the merge rather than added. Composition is unmoved by either sibling: **17 routes on the public surface over four modules, 1 of 17 on the operator surface**. `typecheck` exit 0; `eslint` exit 0; `format:check` clean; invariants **9 of 9**; gates **30 of 30**; `verify` exit 0.

## Session 219: the idempotency layer, the PSP webhook receiver, and an accessor that cannot name a row

**[ADR-109](decisions/ADR-109.md) lands, `status: proposed`, approval line UNSIGNED, MONEY PATH and the `E2` read is owed.** [P3 wave 3](plans/P3-wave3-modules.md)'s `P3-k` is written: [`apps/api/src/idempotency.ts`](../apps/api/src/idempotency.ts), [`apps/api/src/routes/webhooks-psp.ts`](../apps/api/src/routes/webhooks-psp.ts) and **51 tests over two files**, with no migration, no `packages/db` file, no catalog entry and no `routes/index.ts`.

**The slice's dispatch predicted one hole and asked for it to be verified rather than believed. Verifying it found a wider one.** `idempotency_keys` was registered by [session 215](sessions/2026-08-25-session-215.md) as `owned` on a NULLABLE `identity_id`, and **registering it is what created the problem**: `owned` excludes it from `firmDb()`, the nullable column is precisely how the unowned replay is kept out of `scopedDb(identityId)`, and `SystemReason` has two members of which a request handler is neither.

**THE RULING IN ONE LINE IS THAT THE MISSING CONSTRUCTION IS A PREDICATE AND NOT AN AUTHORITY.** `systemDb` gains no third member, because `systemTx.update` passes `undefined` to `updateStatement`'s required `where` position and would write **every row in the table** whatever reason it was handed; `ScopedTx` is blocked identically, narrowing by tenancy and by nothing else. Four of the five available doors fail on the same column of the same table.

| Door | Reaches `idempotency_keys`? | Can name one row? |
|---|---|---|
| `scopedDb(id)` / `scopedTx` | Yes, it is `owned` | **No.** Tenancy predicate only |
| `firmDb()` / `firmTx` | No, `FirmTableKey` excludes `owned` | **No.** No predicate at all |
| `systemDb(reason)` / `systemTx` | Yes, generic over `TableKey` | **No.** No predicate at all |
| A hypothetical `'request-handler'` reason | Yes | **No.** Identical to the row above |
| `sqlExecutor(reason)` | Yes, it is raw SQL | Yes, and its vocabulary is one member and it is not this |

**The remedy the dispatch itself prescribed is unavailable inside the fence.** `sqlExecutor` takes `SqlExecutorReason`, whose type is the single member `'job-enqueue'`, and [`scoped-db.ts:742`](../packages/db/src/scoped-db.ts) **checks it at run time and throws**. Widening it is a `packages/db` edit, which the same dispatch says to report rather than take. **[Session 222](sessions/2026-08-26-session-222.md) hit this wall one day earlier from `apps/worker` and reported it**; this is the second caller, so the ruling is written rather than reported a second time.

**A SECOND RULING ARRIVES FROM THE FRAMEWORK AND IT IS MEASURED RATHER THAN REASONED.** API_CONTRACT section 10 states *"HMAC signature verified BEFORE parsing"* in capitals, and fastify 5.12.1's default `application/json` parser hands a handler a parsed `Object` with `request.raw` already drained, so the ordering is lost before any code of Merit's runs. `{ parseAs: 'buffer' }` recovers the exact bytes and **applies even when registered after the route**, which is what makes the seam small; `RouteDefinition` carries none, and `registry.ts` is outside this fence. **A handler may never recover the bytes by re-encoding `request.body`**: two JSON texts that parse equal serialise differently, so the MAC fails and every legitimate webhook answers `401` with no line of code looking wrong. The suite watches that round trip being refused.

**THERE IS NO UPDATE STATEMENT IN THE RECEIVER AND THAT IS THE DEDUPE WORKING.** The order is apply, then INSERT the row carrying the result the application produced, then ROLL BACK if `psp_webhook_events_provider_event_uq` refused the claim. A duplicate therefore undoes the application and returns `200`, so **one provider event delivered twice produces exactly one business effect and two 200s**. The two responses are byte-identical, which is a control rather than laziness: a response that said "duplicate" would answer which event ids Merit has already seen.

**A landmine is named and not repaired.** `idempotency_keys.key` is the PRIMARY KEY and carries no identity, so one caller's token can block another's on the same endpoint. It is a **denial and not a disclosure**, because the scope predicate keeps the first caller's stored response out of the second's hands, and `beginIdempotent` reports it as its own outcome rather than guessing which of the two cases it is. The repair is a migration and this session is forbidden one.

**What is deliberately not here.** No `@merit/db` dependency in `apps/api`, so the absence is a fact somebody can grep. No production adapter for either provider, because [`packages/psp`](../packages/psp/src/index.ts) ships two fakes and shipping a real one is a procurement decision nobody has taken, so a live deployment answers `503 service_unavailable` and the route is still registered. No re-drive of a deferred event: `defer_attempts` is written `0` and never incremented, because the receiver is the first arrival and the re-driver is the batch's.

**Measured on this branch, not inherited.** Suite **122 files / 2,028 passed / 1 skipped** to **124 files / 2,079 passed / 1 skipped** at base, and **127 files / 2,126 passed / 1 skipped** re-measured after three merges from `main` ([session 224](sessions/2026-08-26-session-224.md), then [session 225](sessions/2026-08-26-session-225.md) with `ADR-110` signed and `ADR-111` returned to the pool). **Session 224's route module and this one share no file**: [ADR-100](decisions/ADR-100.md)'s directory listing composed three modules with no collision and neither branch coordinated with the other; `typecheck` exit 0; `eslint apps/api` exit 0; invariants **9 of 9**; gates **30 of 30**; `verify` exit 0. **Seven mutations seeded and all seven caught**, every seed removed with `git status --porcelain` clean of them. **`0048` stays free and no file under [`packages/db`](../packages/db/src/scoped-db.ts) is touched.**

**Session 220 inherits [ADR-109](decisions/ADR-109.md) clause 2 as a third caller.** `POST /checkout` presents an `Idempotency-Key` that API_CONTRACT section 1 makes REQUIRED, and the layer it presents it to cannot store the response. **NOT MERGED. The `E2` read is owed on every line.**

## Session 226: the portal's last read screens, and a banner that cannot be given the endpoint it needs

**[`P4-h`](plans/P4-portal-and-site.md) is done and [ADR-111](decisions/ADR-111.md) is minted, `status: proposed`, UNSIGNED.** Not a money path: no migration, no `SD-nn`, no `packages/db` import, no write path. Five read screens and the three shapes [session 158](sessions/2026-08-24-session-158.md) found with no contract row at all.

**THE ADR RULES 2 OF 3 BY CONTRACT ROW AND 3 OF 3 BY DISPOSITION, AND THE SPLIT IS THE RULING RATHER THAN A SHORTFALL.**

`EconomicCalendarPanelResponse` enters [API_CONTRACT](architecture/API_CONTRACT.md) as a new **section 6.1**, `GET /economic-calendar`, `Auth: session`. Its shape is the portal type unchanged in a single field, because that type was built column by column off [`0039`](../packages/db/migrations/0039_economic_calendar.sql) against `DEP-M4-09`. **A subsection rather than a new top-level section**: section 12 is addressed BY NUMBER by `CI-06k`, by `DEP-M4-07` and by [ADR-039](decisions/ADR-039.md) amendment 4, so inserting a section ahead of it breaks all three silently, which is [ADR-034](decisions/ADR-034.md)'s drift reached through a heading instead of through a count.

`required_factor` enters **section 2** as `Problem`'s optional extension member over section 12's six-token vocabulary, on a `403` and nowhere else. **Session 218's open pull request already sends exactly that field and does not declare it**: it edits six files and none of them is API_CONTRACT, so the field is shipped and undeclared against an `approved` document. The row makes it legal rather than ruling against a branch in flight, and nothing of that branch was edited.

**AND THE HALF IT DOES NOT DISCHARGE IS STATED RATHER THAN COUNTED AS DONE.** The `403` member discharges section 12 and discharges **neither `DEP-M4-07` nor `INV-M4-14`**, because a field that arrives on a refusal cannot render a control disabled BEFORE the refusal. [M04 section 3.7](plans/M04-trader-portal.md) is written against exactly that: _"A boundary that is only ever discovered by hitting it is indistinguishable from a bug, and users route around bugs."_ The read-surface half belongs to `GET /me`, which is the auth surface's, and [P4](plans/P4-portal-and-site.md) section 6 puts auth in no phase's contents at all.

`ImpersonationSession` is **declared as section 3.2 with no endpoint**, and the section says so in its own text. Its carrier is `Me.impersonation` on `GET /me`, because the banner _"renders from the session the server resolved"_ and a dedicated read is a second session resolution: two resolutions on one page can disagree by the width of a request, which is `GS-301` exactly. `ADMIN_ORIGIN` stays a placeholder ([ADR-012](decisions/ADR-012.md)) and the shape has no field an origin could go in.

**Seven of [M04](plans/M04-trader-portal.md) section 3.1's eleven screens now exist**, against three at [session 158](sessions/2026-08-24-session-158.md). `SC-M4-01`, `SC-M4-04`, `SC-M4-10` and `SC-M4-11` were deliberately not taken and the seams are reported instead.

**Two design rules that came out of the screens and are worth carrying.** The rule diff **renders both sides and no difference**, because every delta is a money value computed client side at the one place the subtraction looks harmless, which is where `INV-M4-01` says the danger is; and the walk is **structural over opaque JSON**, because a typed walk can only compare keys the type knows and would report _"nothing changed"_ about a contract that gained a key, on the screen whose whole job is to be the record of what a trader agreed to.

**One finding for the founder, recorded and not ruled.** [M04:86](plans/M04-trader-portal.md) says `SC-M4-07` shows _"four honest states"_ and `kyc_status` at [`0001:29`](../packages/db/migrations/0001_extensions_and_enums.sql) declares **five**; [API_CONTRACT:517](architecture/API_CONTRACT.md) types the field as an open `string` and settles nothing. The screen is built against the five, because the enum is what will actually arrive and a view handling four of five renders the fifth as nothing.

**`surface.test.ts`'s `purchase` entry was NARROWED and not deleted**, to `checkout`, `reset` and `acknowledg`. That is [session 158](sessions/2026-08-24-session-158.md)'s own test of a good amendment (_"a session that deletes an entry instead of narrowing it has removed the control while appearing to satisfy it"_), and the narrowed list is strictly stronger on the write path: `purchase` would never have caught `submitCheckout`.

## Session 227: the accessor learns to name ONE ROW, and the six writes that could not are removed

**[ADR-112](decisions/ADR-112.md) lands, `status: proposed`, approval line UNSIGNED. MONEY PATH and the `E2` read is owed on every line.** [ADR-109](decisions/ADR-109.md) clause 2 said the accessor needs a keyed read and a keyed write and refused to design it, because the shape decides whether *"reach the database and choose a scope are the SAME ACT"* survives. **The founder delegated that design authority to this session and delegated the `E2` read to nobody.**

**THE DEFECT HAD NO REAL CALLERS AND THAT IS WHY A BROKEN METHOD COULD BE DELETED RATHER THAN DEPRECATED.** Re-measured rather than trusted: outside `packages/db` itself, every mention of `systemTx.update`, `firmTx.update` and `scopedTx.update` in the tree is a COMMENT routing around it, and the only real invocations of a transaction handle's methods are two `.rows(...)` reads in [`packages/ledger`](../packages/ledger/src/chart.ts) and three `.insert(...)`. **So `ScopedTx.update`, `ScopedTx.delete`, `SystemTx.update`, `SystemTx.delete`, `FirmTx.update` and `FirmTx.delete` no longer exist**, and [ADR-042](decisions/ADR-042.md)'s finding that a comment is not a control is why they are not left behind one. `rows` and `insert` are unchanged, so [`packages/ledger`](../packages/ledger/src/tx.ts) is untouched and its cross-package bind assertion still passes.

**THE FOUR RULINGS.**

| # | Ruled | On what evidence |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | **A predicate is a TYPED EQUALITY over declared columns, never a `SQL` fragment** | A `SQL` parameter hands every call site the surface [ADR-008](decisions/ADR-008.md) scoped the accessor to bound, and reads like ordinary accessor use rather than like the raw SQL it is. `byId(id)` is refused ON EVIDENCE: `idempotency_keys`' primary key is `key`, and **13 registered tables declare a composite one** |
| 2 | **A WRITE takes an address containing a unique key the schema declares; a READ may take a plain filter** | A filtered read is a NARROWING of a read that already exists at the same authority, so it grants no reach. A filtered write at non-unique columns is the defect returning at a smaller radius |
| 3 | **The columns the HANDLE PINS are both the columns the caller may not name and the columns that count toward the key** | One set, two consequences. The predicate that reaches the database is the COMPOSITION |
| 4 | **The tenancy narrowing and the address COMPOSE, and the wrong shape does not compile** | The write predicate is two disjoint branded types with one producer each. **A keyed write that DROPS TENANCY is `TS2345`**, not a test somebody has to keep |

**TWO DESIGN ERRORS WERE FOUND BY ONE COVERAGE ASSERTION RATHER THAN BY READING, AND BOTH ARE RECORDED BECAUSE THE REASONING THAT PRODUCED THEM WILL BE REPEATED.** Requiring the CALLER's half of the predicate to contain a unique key left `notification_preferences`, `wallet_spend_limits`, `loyalty_states` and `discord_links` unaddressable, because their primary key is `(identity_id, ...)` and the caller is refused `identity_id`. Refusing a scoped caller naming a `derived` rule's local column left `analytics_snapshots` unaddressable, because its key is `(account_id, as_of_trading_day)` and an `EXISTS` over `accounts` pins neither: one identity owns many accounts. **Under the ruling as it stands, all 60 scoped tables have a reachable address.**

**THE ADDRESSABILITY CLAIM IS FOLDED AGAINST ALL 47 MIGRATIONS IN THE DIRECTION THAT CAN HURT, AND THAT SET IS EMPTY.** An address is admitted because its columns carry a key the DATABASE enforces, and what a runtime can read is [`schema.ts`](../packages/db/src/schema.ts), which is a transcription somebody keeps true by hand. **Zero column sets the schema declares unique are absent from the DDL**; the reverse direction is 34 keys and is fail-closed, asserted as a PROPERTY rather than as a count. **`treasury_balances` is its extreme case**: [`0009_ledger.sql`](../packages/db/migrations/0009_ledger.sql) gives it `PRIMARY KEY (account_code, as_of)` and the schema declares none, so it is the one registered table of 104 with no addressed write at all. `schema.ts` is outside this fence, so the suite pins that set to exactly one table and the repair is one line elsewhere. **A PARTIAL unique index is not read as a key**, and `provisioning_queue_intent_uq` is the live counter-example.

**WHAT WAS WATCHED.** Eight runtime mutations seeded and all eight caught, the widest being `handlePinnedColumns` reading nothing at **9 red** -- which is [ADR-102](decisions/ADR-102.md)'s own warning executed, that a guard with nothing to find looks exactly like a guard finding nothing wrong. Seven compile refusals watched failing by their error. **The round trip EXECUTED**: all 47 migrations applied on PostgreSQL 16, ten cases, and **row 3 is the approval line -- a keyed update through `scopedDb(A)` naming `B`'s row writes ZERO rows and leaves that row unchanged**, while row 7 shows one address through two handles reaching two different rows on the composite-key class.

**WHAT IS DELIBERATELY NOT HERE.** `AuthBackend` is not wired and `IdempotencyStore` is not implemented: this session builds the construction they were blocked on, not the callers. [`index.ts`](../packages/db/src/index.ts) is outside the fence and is not edited, which costs nothing today because the methods are reachable without naming their types, and costs the first caller that wants to declare one a single export line. **No migration. `0048` stays free.**

**Measured on this branch rather than inherited.** Suite **128 files / 2,170 passed / 1 skipped** to **129 files / 2,193 passed / 1 skipped**; `packages/db` **9 files / 407 passed** to **10 files / 431 passed**; `typecheck` exit 0; `eslint packages/db` exit 0; invariants **9 of 9**; gates **30 of 30**; `verify` exit 0. **The corpus now owes ELEVEN permanent compile refusals**, four from [ADR-102](decisions/ADR-102.md) and seven from here, each watched once by the session that wrote it and never again; [`falsify-ci.mjs`](../scripts/ci/falsify-ci.mjs) is where they belong and it is outside every one of those fences. **NOT MERGED.**

## Session 229: `RI-08`, the invariant [ADR-096](decisions/ADR-096.md) named and nobody wrote

**[ADR-117](decisions/ADR-117.md) lands, `status: proposed`, approval line UNSIGNED. NOT MONEY PATH by file, and the hole it closes is a money-path hole.** No ledger, no payout, no engine, no auth, no migration; `git status --porcelain packages/db apps` is zero on the branch. What it guards is the [ADR-008](decisions/ADR-008.md) BOLA blast radius `scopedDb` exists to bound, approached from the manifest rather than from the type.

**THREE ENTRIES HAD CITED THIS HOLE AND NONE HAD CLOSED IT.** [ADR-096](decisions/ADR-096.md) section 9 named `RI-08`, measured it and assigned it to `P4-e`; `P4-e` landed without it; [ADR-095](decisions/ADR-095.md)'s `F4` and its section 9 item 5b name the same gap from the framework side. The hole in ADR-096's words: *"A marketing page can acquire a write-capable connection to the trader database in a one-line manifest diff, and every check in this repository stays green while it happens."*

**THE ONLY THING RULED IS THE SCOPE, AND IT IS A WIDENING OF A SIGNED ENTRY ON EVIDENCE THAT ARRIVED AFTER IT.** ADR-096 scopes the check to `apps/site`, widens itself one sentence later to `packages/queue` and calls the wider version *"the better version of it"*; ADR-095 item 5b names the same under-scoping, *"it reads `apps/site` where `F4`'s subject is `M04:25`, which is `apps/portal`"*. **FIVE manifests now state `@merit/db`'s absence as a design property where ADR-096 counted two** ([`queue`](../packages/queue/package.json), [`ledger`](../packages/ledger/package.json), [`psp`](../packages/psp/package.json), [`apps/api`](../apps/api/package.json), [`apps/site`](../apps/site/package.json)), **and ZERO packages in this workspace declare it in any dependency field.** So the check guards EVERY workspace package against an admission list that is **EMPTY**, which is `onlyBuiltDependencies: []`'s shape, `.npmrc`'s argument and [ADR-084](decisions/ADR-084.md) section 5's *"a list somebody has to join"*. **`apps/api` is NOT pre-admitted** though [ADR-109](decisions/ADR-109.md) says it will need the accessor first: a list that admits against an unstated need is a list joining itself. **`RI-10` is the reason the scope is not two names**: its first draft excluded a package BY NAME, and a check that needs a name-based exception is usually scoped wrong.

**THE MANIFEST GATE WAS MEASURED IN BOTH DIRECTIONS AND IT CONTRADICTS A LINE IN THE TREE.** [`.npmrc`](../.npmrc)'s `node-linker=isolated` makes an undeclared import unresolvable at run time. **It does not resolve at build time either**: seeded once into `apps/site/src` and once into `apps/api/src`, with no `paths` mapping anywhere, both report `error TS2307: Cannot find module '@merit/db'`. **So the manifest field is not merely where the dependency is recorded; it is the only place the capability can be acquired**, which is why `RI-08` has no source half. [`apps/api/package.json:15`](../apps/api/package.json)'s *"`tsc` resolves it happily through the workspace"* is **wrong on this tree**; its conclusion survives and its reason does not. Out of fence, unedited, reported.

**THREE READINGS OF "RESOLVES TO THE ACCESSOR", EACH SEEDED ON THE REAL TREE AND WATCHED FAILING, AND TWO NEAR-MISSES WATCHED STAYING SILENT.** The key, a `workspace:`/`npm:` alias parsed out rather than substring-matched, and a `link:` path that **writes the accessor's name nowhere** and is invisible to a name test of any kind. Silent on `@merit/dbtools`, the substring trap, and on an ordinary workspace dependency. **THEN FALSIFIED**, which is `RI-10`'s landmine paid off: with the `acquires` helper neutered the six detection cases go red and the two silence cases stay green. **TWO GUARDS THROW RATHER THAN PASS AND BOTH ARE ABOUT THE ADMISSION LIST**, because that is the direction this check gets weakened in: nobody deletes an invariant, somebody admits one more package each time one is inconvenient. A stale name throws; a list covering every package throws with *"asserting nothing"*.

**[ALLOCATION](decisions/ALLOCATION.md) GAINS A FIFTH TABLE, FOR `RI-nn`, AND IT IS AN ALLOCATOR AND SAYS SO.** An invariant number gets claimed in ADR prose where a grep for the next free number does not look; `RI-08` sat claimed and unwritten for eight days and `RI-10` was taken the same way, which is `OI-27`'s class. The rows are READ from the `CHECKS` array, so `RI-04`'s and `RI-09`'s computed titles move without an edit. **It is NOT the `RI` series repair**: `gates.mjs`'s `PENDING_SERIES` names the tooling README as `RI`'s register, that README's table stops at `RI-05` and is out of fence, so the pending entry stands. **`CI-06/identifier-series` was probed in BOTH shapes before the table was written**, ten rows and five, and both reported 30 of 30, with the probes removed and the tree clean after.

**FOUR FINDINGS REPORTED RATHER THAN TAKEN**, each somebody else's fence: `apps/api`'s stale `tsc` sentence; a raw driver DECLARED in a manifest and not yet imported, which nothing refuses because `merit/no-raw-db-client` reads source; [`packages/tooling/README.md`](../packages/tooling/README.md)'s invariant table stopping at `RI-05` and calling `RI-04` *"four deployables"* when `DEPLOYABLES` holds five; and [`falsify-ci.mjs`](../scripts/ci/falsify-ci.mjs) having an `RI-01` case and no `RI-08` one.

**Measured on this branch rather than inherited.** **10 of 10 invariants hold** (9 of 9 before), **30 of 30 gates pass**, suite **134 files / 2,256 passed / 1 skipped**, `pnpm run verify` **exit 0**, `git status --porcelain` clean. **NOT MERGED.**

## The two owed gates, and a proposed discriminator that was measured and replaced (2026-08-26, session 230)

**Two gates land. `gate_count` was 30 when this session opened and is now <!--gen:gate_count-->32<!--/gen--> in every span that carries it, rewritten by `gates.mjs generate` rather than by hand.** [ADR-118](decisions/ADR-118.md) at `status: proposed`, approval line **UNSIGNED**, one clause, executable, scoped to this branch's files. Not a money path. No migration, no `CI-06` letter, and the letter allocation table is untouched.

### `CI-06/table-row-width`, and why the check the pull request proposed is not the check that shipped

[PR #299](https://github.com/lam2-coder/meritfutures/pull/299) repaired [`docs/sessions/README.md`](sessions/README.md) after a row insertion landed past the reservation table's terminating blank line and a prettier run absorbed **nine prose lines into the table as rows**, with first cells like _"lands, its entry joins the list below"_. **All 30 gates stayed green**, and the reason is precise: `CI-06u` looks for DUPLICATE first cells and nine prose lines are all distinct, `CI-06v` looks for ORPHAN runs and these sat inside a well formed table. **Neither gate asks whether a row BELONGS.**

**#299's proposed check was "a first cell not shaped like the table's key column". It was surveyed against every table under `docs/` before anything was written, and it does not survive the survey.**

| Rule | Tables it reaches | Rows to register on a clean tree | Does it catch #299 |
|---|---|---|---|
| First-cell shape, 80% homogeneity | **593 of 1,593** multi-row tables | 25 | **NO.** Eight absorbed rows drag the reservation table to **27 of 35** conforming, which is 0.77, so the table falls out of scope and the gate goes quiet on the defect it was proposed for |
| First-cell shape, 50% homogeneity | 593 in scope, 67 with outliers | **155, in 67 tables** | Yes, at a price that is furniture within a month |
| **Cell count** | **1,604 of 1,604**, no shape exemption of any kind | **17** | **Yes, all eight rows** |

**So the discriminator is the cell count and `RI-10`'s lesson is what decided it**: a check that needs a name-based exception is usually scoped wrong, and this one needs no exception. The delimiter row is the authority, which is GitHub-flavoured markdown's own rule, and both directions are findings: a SHORT row is #299's absorbed prose rendering as empty cells, a LONG row has its excess **silently discarded** on render.

**THE SEVENTEEN ARE REAL AND SIX OF THEM ARE IN [`ALLOCATION`](decisions/ALLOCATION.md)'S OWN ADR TABLE.** Rows `079`, `088`, `095`, `104`, `112` and `0046` carry a fourth cell in a three-column table, so a whole disposition paragraph -- in the registry a sibling branch reads to decide whether a number is free -- is invisible to every reader of the rendered file. **This session held one row of that file and took only that row**, so they are registered rather than repaired, and the register shrinks only.

### `CI-06/derivable-counts`, the sweep `CI-06g` has declared owed in its own words since it was written

`CI-06g`'s `covers` line has read _"the corpus-wide sweep for bare numerals adjacent to a registry noun needs the generator and is NOT run here"_ since the day it landed, and [ADR-034](decisions/ADR-034.md) recorded that the sweep _"is the gate's first run and is not done here"_. The generator exists. **The receipt is the session 204 integration, recorded above: tranche A raised `schema.ts`'s drifted-table sentence to NINE for `payout_requests`, tranche B raised it to NINE for `promotional_credit_grants`, git saw no conflict because both sides wrote the same character, and the answer was TEN.**

**Enforcing ADR-034 literally is not possible and the number that says so is 206.** Measured over every markdown file under `docs/` with the reader that shipped: a cardinal governing a registry noun at ANY value is **1,677 sites**, of which **206 are in live prose** and almost every one is a local subset -- `1 gate`, `2 gate`, `Six deltas`, `three tables`. A totality word before the cardinal gives **five** findings in live prose and **all five are false**. Value-anchoring -- the cardinal must equal what its bound query returns on this tree -- gives **zero**, with 137 sites under a dated or session heading and 11 in table rows, both excluded by shape and both printed on every run.

**[ADR-118](decisions/ADR-118.md) is what that exclusion costs and it is a ruling rather than an implementation note.** A section headed by a date or a session number is a RECORD of a measurement made that day; _"all 47 migrations applied in order"_ was true when it was written, and a generated span there would rewrite the record to say something it did not say. **The false negative is accepted in writing: a count that has ALREADY drifted is invisible.** On the merged tree the receipt read NINE against a truth of TEN and this gate would have been silent. On either branch alone it read NINE against a derivation of NINE and is named there, **while it is still right, which is the only moment a span can be installed without anybody adjudicating the truth.**

### Two findings recorded rather than repaired, and one of them no gate in this runner can see

- **[`STRATEGY`](testing/STRATEGY.md) carries a byte-identical DUPLICATED PROSE LINE at 271 and 272.** `CI-06u` reads table rows, `CI-06v` reads pipe runs, and a repeated paragraph is neither. It is a keep-both merge artifact of exactly the class `CI-06u` exists for, one layer out, and it is a candidate for a third gate. **Not repaired: session 231 holds that file tonight.**
- **Three of the seventeen registered ragged rows are GENERATED**, built by the `session_entries` span from a session log's own `<!--index:` line, where a pipe inside an inline code span splits the row and drops its tail. **The repair is the generator and not the rows**, and it is owed.

**ONE DEFECT IN THE NEW GATE IS RECORDED RATHER THAN QUIETLY FIXED, because the harness could not see it.** The first reader captured the noun with a lazy `[A-Za-z ]*?` and a word-boundary lookahead, which stops at the FIRST word, so `edge cases` was read as `edge` and **three of the eight vocabulary entries could never match anything**. The gate reported PASS on a clean tree, correctly, while asserting five eighths of what its `covers` line claimed, and every scope case passed because every one of them used the single word `gates`. **Found by re-reading the regex, not by `falsify.mjs`.** The repair anchors each vocabulary pattern against the text; `CI-06/derivable-counts/a-two-word-noun-is-one-noun` now watches the branch. **A vocabulary of eight entries is not one code path watched eight times**, and that is the general form of the lesson.

### What is owed, named rather than left to be rediscovered

How many registered tables carry a later `ADD COLUMN` is derived by [`scoped-db.test.ts`](../packages/db/test/scoped-db.test.ts)'s replay and by nothing in `gates.mjs`, so the gate reaches the CLASS and not that INSTANCE.
- **A comment-span generator, so source files come into scope.** The same reader over every `.ts`, `.tsx`, `.mjs` and `.sql` finds **17 sites**, eleven under `packages/` -- four in [`schema.ts`](../packages/db/src/schema.ts) and three in [`scope.ts`](../packages/db/src/scope.ts) -- and six in the runner and its own harness. They are out of scope today because `generate()` rewrites markdown only, and **a finding with no remedy is how a gate gets switched off.**

**The position:** `node scripts/corpus/gates.mjs check` reports <!--gen:gate_count-->32<!--/gen--> of <!--gen:gate_count-->32<!--/gen--> passing. `node scripts/corpus/falsify.mjs` reports every gate passing clean and failing dirty with **81 scope cases** (70 before) and 10 loader cases. `pnpm run check:invariants` reports 9 of 9 and `pnpm run verify` exits 0. **`CI-06/table-row-width`'s seed replays #299's edit on the live document rather than pasting its output**, so a rewording announces itself as a stale seed instead of quietly reproducing nothing. **[ADR-118](decisions/ADR-118.md)'s clause was EXECUTED before the entry was written**: that edit on a copy of this tree gives **31 PASS, 1 FAIL, 0 ERROR**, and the one failure names all eight absorbed rows. The 31 are what happened on `main`.

## `CI-09`'s replay leg has an INPUT, and the gate that watched for it is RED on purpose (2026-08-26, session 231)

**[ADR-119](decisions/ADR-119.md), `status: proposed`, unsigned.** The artifact [STRATEGY section 4.1](testing/STRATEGY.md) has called *"a demo-world seed script"* since 2026-08-20 is ruled to be **[`scripts/demo/world.ts`](../scripts/demo/world.ts)**, a path. [Session 121](sessions/2026-08-21-session-121.md) rowed it *"Registered. Names neither a path nor a manifest key"*, `CI-06/gate-inventory` reported it unprobeable on every run since, and **naming the path was the ruling**: a session that invented one would have closed a registered condition by fiat, which is what [ADR-073](decisions/ADR-073.md) section 2 (b) exists to prevent. **The unprobeable register goes from four entries to three**, and the three that remain are `CI-04`'s Neon branch, the `VG-12` admission and M07's detector code. Two of those three are estate or a human decision and no ruling can give either a path; **M07's detector code is the only one a future ADR can re-rule the way this one did.**

**THE WORLD IS A VALUE AND NOT A POSTGRES SEED, on two measurements either of which is enough.** Nothing in this tree reads a database into `BatchPorts`, which [`apps/worker/src/index.ts`](../apps/worker/src/index.ts) already says about itself, so rows seeded into `rule_states` today reach `runReplayAudit` **through nothing at all**. And `rule_states` has no column for `lifetimeSettledCents`, `breached` or `breachKind`, so `AccountDay.prior` could not be read back out of storage even once an adapter is written. **A database seed would have given the replay leg a SUBJECT and still no INPUT**, which is [session 118](sessions/2026-08-20-session-118.md)'s own distinction one level down. **[INFRA section 11](architecture/INFRA.md)'s seed script is a second, different artifact**, it is unbuilt, and ADR-119 clause 3 says so, so that nobody reads either as having satisfied the other.

**WHAT RAN.** The world is **6 accounts over 25 weekday sessions, 94 stored rows, 3 funded and 3 breached**, folded through `foldAccountDay` and hashed by `stateHash`, which is the row the nightly batch would have written. `runReplayAudit` over it reports **`matched: 94, diverged: 0, outOfScope: 0`**, against an expectation the seed counted **before** the audit ran. Then one cent is added to one stored row's `balance_cents`, **with the hash recomputed over the wrong value**, and the audit reports exactly one divergence naming that column. Leaving the hash alone would have left the stored bytes agreeing with the replay and proved the opposite of what the case looks like; it was checked by running it, and four of the sixteen committed cases go red. **This is the first time INV-04 has been asserted over a world in this repository.**

**THE GATE IS RED AND THAT IS THE CONDITION WORKING.** `gates` reports **29 of 30**, with two findings on `CI-06/gate-inventory`, both predicted before the row was edited: the probe table refuses to grow itself ([ADR-074](decisions/ADR-074.md) section 2), and the register entry for the old wording now names no live condition. **A third arrives after the probe does** and stands until the workflow job lands. **Two red, then one red, then green.** `pnpm run verify` therefore does not exit 0 on that branch and cannot; every other stage is green on its own (`check:invariants` 9 of 9, `typecheck`, `lint`, `format:check`, `vitest run` **135 files / 2,260 passed / 1 skipped**). **`falsify` reports three problems and all three are one root cause**, measured both ways: with the row reverted it is 30 gates clean and dirty, 70 scope cases and zero problems.

**FOUR THINGS OWED, and ADR-119 section 6 names each with its owner.** The probe in [`gates.mjs`](../scripts/corpus/gates.mjs) (**session 230 holds `scripts/corpus` tonight; reported as a collision rather than resolved**); the `replay-self-audit` job in [`nightly.yml`](../.github/workflows/nightly.yml), whose whole body is `node scripts/demo/seed-world.mjs`, and which should land in the same branch as the probe so the gate crosses once; the `accountsAudited === 0` refusal moving from the seed runner into `replay.ts`, which was outside this fence; and `OI-14`'s row in [`DELTA_MANIFEST`](../packages/db/DELTA_MANIFEST.md), which now has a caller that fires the refusal it allocates.

**ONE FINDING WORTH MORE THAN THE SCRIPT, handed on rather than repaired.** `runNightlyBatch` **cannot drive a world more than one trading day deep**: its report carries `row` and `events` and not `state`, and `RuleStateRow` cannot rebuild a `RuleState` for the three-column reason above. That is why the seed calls `foldAccountDay`. **The production consequence is larger than the seed's**: `loadAccountDay` has no source for `AccountDay.prior` either, so **the `BatchPorts` adapter this repository has been waiting for since session 147 cannot be written against the schema as it stands.** It needs a ruling on whether the three fields are stored, derived or excluded. **No migration was written and `0048` stays free.** **NOT MERGED.**
