## Session 220: checkout and attribution, and the wall ADR-112 moved half of

**[ADR-113](decisions/ADR-113.md) lands, `status: proposed`, approval line UNSIGNED. MONEY PATH and the `E2` read is owed on every line.** `POST /checkout` and `POST /accounts/:accountId/reset` exist, the price comes from `plan_version_sizes` and never from the request, the coupon discount is recomputed server side, and **attribution resolves INSIDE the checkout transaction** ([M08](plans/M08-affiliate-system.md) section 3.1), which is why `P3-n` was one slice rather than two.

**THE DISPATCH'S HEADLINE IS HALF RIGHT AND THIS ENTRY SAYS WHICH HALF.** [ADR-112](decisions/ADR-112.md) gave the accessor an ADDRESS and its own section 10 says it did not move the AUTHORITY. `attributions` is scope class `pair` ([`scope.ts:1067`](../packages/db/src/scope.ts)); a `pair` key is in **neither** `ScopedTableKey` nor `FirmTableKey` ([ADR-106](decisions/ADR-106.md)); `SystemReason` is `'nightly-batch' | 'operator-console'` ([`scoped-db.ts:176`](../packages/db/src/scoped-db.ts)). **A checkout request handler is none of the three.** [Session 216](sessions/2026-08-25-session-216.md) reported the shape from the ledger and [session 215](sessions/2026-08-25-session-215.md) attached this table to it by name. **It is reported and not taken here**, because a third door on the money path is not a checkout slice's to open, and `CheckoutTx.insertAttribution` is the port where the decision lands.

**`IdempotencyStore` IS RULED THE NEXT SESSION'S, ON THE FENCE RATHER THAN ON PREFERENCE, AND [ADR-109](decisions/ADR-109.md) CLAUSE 3 STANDS UNCHANGED.** ADR-112 removed the obstacle that clause named. What it did not remove is that an implementation must import `@merit/db` into `apps/api`, whose manifest declares no such dependency and was not in this fence. **A one-line manifest edit that makes the deployable serving the whole public surface able to reach a pool is not a side effect of a checkout slice**, and it drags the `pair` question above in with it the moment the first caller writes `attributions`. So **`Idempotency-Key` is REQUIRED by API_CONTRACT section 1 on both endpoints this session landed and neither handler reads it**, which is stated here rather than implied by an absent check.

**API_CONTRACT SECTION 12's CHECKOUT ROW IS ASSERTED IN BOTH DIRECTIONS, AND THE TWO SEEDS ARE NOT THE SAME SIZE.** The row is *"Checkout with a client-supplied price field -> field ignored; server price used"*. A body carrying `amount_cents` is charged the server's price, and the honest path produces the price the server computed from the same seed. **The tampering seed turns 1 assertion red and the seed that makes the price lookup return zero turns 13**, which measures exactly how much of this suite would still pass against a checkout that priced everything at zero. That is why the quiet direction is asserted.

**THE PRICE IS NOT DEFENDED BY A CHECK. IT IS DEFENDED BY HAVING NO PATH FROM THE BODY.** INV-M3-02's enforcement column is the design: *"Zod schema has no price field at all. THE ABSENCE IS THE CONTROL."* The validators build their value field by field and never spread, so an invented key reaches nothing that could read it.

**ELEVEN MUTATIONS SEEDED AND ALL ELEVEN CAUGHT**, each reverted against a byte-identical copy with `md5sum -c` clean before the next. **Six turn exactly one assertion red and are recorded as thin rather than rounded up.** The two worth the most are the pair above and **a post-write refusal RETURNED rather than thrown, at 12 red**: the coupon-claim conflict is decided after the purchase row is inserted, so the refusal is thrown out of the transaction and the rollback is the transaction's own act rather than a compensating delete.

**A THIRD PARTY IS CALLED INSIDE AN OPEN TRANSACTION AND BOTH ALTERNATIVES WERE PRICED RATHER THAN THE HAZARD BEING ROUTED AROUND.** `purchases.psp_reference` is `NOT NULL` and is the webhook idempotency anchor, and M03 section 6 requires `purchase.paid` to match a row Merit created at checkout by `(psp, psp_reference)`. Stamping the reference afterwards needs a nullable column and a migration, and **`0048` stays free**; committing first leaves a `pending` purchase with no payment session whenever the provider is slow.

**THE PSP IS A FAKE AND THE ROUTE SAYS SO WITH A STATUS CODE.** `packages/psp` ships a port and two fakes and no vendor, so a live deployment answers `503 service_unavailable`. The suite proves the pipeline and **shipping this to a real customer needs a procurement decision nobody has taken.**

Both are right about different moments, so the response carries `required_disclosure` as a separate field from the creative's own absent `disclosure_version_id`. **The operator half is owed and is named** rather than left to be discovered: approve, reject, withdraw, and M08 section 3.3's automatic withdrawal have a table, an invariant and no contract.

**ONE FILE OUTSIDE THE FENCE, FORCED AND NAMED IN THE PLAN COMMIT BEFORE IT WAS TOUCHED.** `apps/api/package.json` gains `"@merit/affiliate": "workspace:*"`, because the dispatch puts the fold in the package rather than the handler and `.npmrc`'s `node-linker=isolated` makes an undeclared import unresolvable at run time. ## Session 221: M19 KYC, the composite trigger set, and a contractual anchor that names no table

**[ADR-114](decisions/ADR-114.md) lands, `status: proposed`, approval line UNSIGNED. MONEY PATH and the `E2` read is owed on every line.** [P3 wave 3](plans/P3-wave3-modules.md)'s `P3-o` is written: [`packages/kyc`](../packages/kyc/src/index.ts) (the vendor-agnostic provider port, ADR-021's trigger set, the document screen, one fake), [`routes/kyc.ts`](../apps/api/src/routes/kyc.ts), [`routes/webhooks-kyc.ts`](../apps/api/src/routes/webhooks-kyc.ts) and **133 assertions over five new files**, with no migration, no `packages/db` file and no `routes/index.ts`.

**THE PLACEMENT WAS NOT RE-DECIDED AND THE TWO THINGS IT LEFT OPEN WERE.** [ADR-021](decisions/ADR-021.md) ruled the composite set and the FREEZE gate ruled `{second_distinct_account_purchase, pre_funded}` with the earliest firing. What neither could see is that **"earliest" is a statement about TIME and a gate evaluates a SNAPSHOT**. The tie inside one evaluation is broken by FUNNEL ORDER, which the corpus already writes three times and all three agree, and **the tie-break is sound only because every condition in the set is MONOTONE**: a purchase count never falls, an evaluation pass is latched, and the distinct-account count is a HIGH-WATER count rather than a live one, because a fleet operator who closes an account has still been a second-account holder. **That last line is the one most likely to be quietly reversed by whoever writes the query**, since "how many accounts does this trader have" is the natural question and it is the wrong one. Four properties over 500 generated cases each carry the claim no type can state.

**THE CONTRACT'S IDEMPOTENCY ANCHOR FOR THIS ENDPOINT NAMES NOTHING, AND THREE FACTS SAY SO.** [API_CONTRACT:718](architecture/API_CONTRACT.md) anchors `POST /webhooks/kyc/:provider` on *"`provider_applicant_id` plus event id"*. **There is no `kyc_webhook_events` table**: over all 47 migrations the only inbound-webhook table is `psp_webhook_events`, and its `purchase_id` foreign key makes it the payment rail's. **The pair is not a unique key and must never become one**, because `SD-M19-01` and `INV-M19-06` make a re-verification a NEW ROW against the same applicant, so [ADR-112](decisions/ADR-112.md)'s address refusal is **correct here on a table nobody had checked** rather than a transcription gap. **And no authority admits the caller**: a webhook carries no identity, `kyc_verifications` is `owned`, and the system reasons are two. So the store is a port, `productionDeps` resolves nothing, and the migration is a later session's. **`0048` stays free.**

**ONE ORDERING RULE IS NOW IMPLEMENTED TWICE AND A TYPE IS WHY.** `packages/psp`'s `HmacWebhookScheme` declares `readonly psp: PspId`, closed at two members by a CHECK on `purchases.psp`, so calling it from an identity path would write a payment provider's id into a KYC verification. `kyc_verifications.provider` carries **no CHECK at all**, because naming a vendor is a disclosure event under [ADR-021](decisions/ADR-021.md). The two verifiers are bound by a suite that **reads `packages/psp/src/webhook.ts`** and compares the refusal vocabulary member for member and the ordering step for step, inside the verify function's own body rather than over the file. What would end the duplication is a third package neither provider set brands, and it is priced in ADR-114 section 4.

**MERIT NEVER PROXIES A DOCUMENT, AND THE INVARIANT IS ENFORCED IN TWO PLACES BECAUSE ONE OF THEM CANNOT SEE INSIDE A JSONB BLOB.** The port has no method returning a document and no field one could be assigned to. The receiver SCREENS a verified payload before anything stores it, **REFUSES rather than redacts** because a redaction would leave operators believing their provider is configured the way the privacy policy says, and records **key paths and never values**. The screen's word list is deliberately short and `face_match_score` passes: `dedupe_matches.evidence_snapshot` holds *"scores, method, timestamps. NEVER images"*, so a screen that refused a score would refuse the one payload M19 exists to record.

**FOURTEEN SEEDED MUTATIONS AND ALL FOURTEEN CAUGHT**, including the latest-instead-of-earliest firing at **7 red**, a missing `kyc.triggers` falling back to the frozen set at **4 red**, and the allowlist bypassed so the vendor's rejection reason serialises at **3 red**. Two defects the suite found in this session's own first draft are recorded rather than smoothed over: the fail-closed backend reached the framework as a **500** because `endpointHandler` catches only auth's own unwired error, and the registered production webhook route answers **404 and not the 503 its header claimed**, because the resolver runs before the store check.

**Measured on this branch rather than inherited.** Suite to **139 files / 2,377 passed / 1 skipped**; `typecheck`, `lint` and `format:check` exit 0; invariants **9 of 9**; gates **30 of 30**; `verify` exit 0; `falsify` clean-and-dirty over all 30 gates, 70 scope cases and 10 loader cases. **Two files outside the fence**, `apps/api/package.json` and `pnpm-lock.yaml`, eighteen lines all of them importer blocks and none a `packages:` entry, and **the same two files collide with sessions 220 and 223**, which create packages under the same constraint with neither file in their fences. Reported rather than resolved. **NOT MERGED.**

**`CI-05` WENT RED ON THE FIRST PUSH AND `verify` COULD NOT HAVE CAUGHT IT.** `gitleaks`' `generic-api-key` rule read one line of a KYC test fixture as a credential: a real base64 image header bound to a local variable named `secret`. It was a fake document, in the test that proves the document screen reports **paths and never values**, and the assertion needs a value that must not travel rather than one that looks like a key. **The literal is described here and NOT reproduced, and the first draft of this paragraph reproduced it**, which turned `CI-05` red a second time with two findings in the commit that recorded the first. That is the document screen's own rule (*"a finding that quoted it would carry the document into the log line reporting it"*) written into code by this session and then broken in prose by the same session, one commit later. **The local `verify` runs none of the four `CI-05` scanners by design**, so green locally says nothing about that stage. **The half worth carrying is the second one: a forward commit CANNOT clear a `gitleaks` finding.** `gitleaks git .` scans commit PATCHES, so a finding lives in the patch that introduced it and survives every later commit that removes the line; the working-tree scan (`gitleaks dir .`) goes clean immediately and reports the opposite of the truth. Measured at all three points with the pinned `8.30.1` binary whose tarball digest matches `ci.yml`'s pin byte for byte: red before, **still red after the forward fix**, clean only after the branch's history was rewritten. **A session that fixed the line, saw the directory scan go clean and pushed would have left the stage red without knowing why**, and merging it would have carried the leaking patch into `main`, since this repository merges with a merge commit rather than a squash. The repair was a rebase plus `git push --force-with-lease`, which is the line [`.claude/hooks/block-dangerous-shell.mjs`](../.claude/hooks/block-dangerous-shell.mjs) already draws: it refuses `--force` and permits `--force-with-lease`, *"because the lease is precisely the property the ban on force-push exists to obtain"*. **The founder was asked before it was run**, and the alternative considered and rejected was a `.gitleaksignore` fingerprint, which buys green by keeping the thing that should not be there.

## ADR-023 enrichment lands in OBSERVE MODE, and the two places it could quietly become enforcement are closed by shape (2026-08-26, session 223)

**[`packages/enrichment`](../packages/enrichment/package.json) is new and it decides nothing.** [ADR-023](decisions/ADR-023.md) is accepted and is not reopened: the vendor is bought and not built, the adapter is vendor-agnostic, the rollout is graduated, and step 1 is observe mode, "signals recorded, scored, and reported; nothing is blocked". What the transcription had to settle is [ADR-115](decisions/ADR-115.md), `status: proposed`, approval line UNSIGNED. **MONEY PATH BY POSITION and the `E2` read is owed.**

**THE SCORE HAS NO PERSISTED COLUMN AND ONE IS NOT INVENTED.** There is no column anywhere in the 47 migrations for an observe-mode enrichment score. The only available surface is `risk_flags`, whose `source` column is reserved `'vendor:<name>'` in its own DDL comment "so a QuantSentry-class detector plugs in without a migration", and taking that invitation up would hand an untuned score authority over [ADR-040](decisions/ADR-040.md)'s `G-HOLD-REQUIRED`, which holds a payout on an unresolved severity-4 flag, while `OQ-M3-03` is still open on whether the same band may stop a purchase. **`D-12` already ruled the shape for a detector that observes without accusing**: "Output is a watched-cluster set, not a flag ... rather than accusing anyone." So no flag is written, the score is REPORTED and not STORED, and the migration that would store it is specified in [ADR-115](decisions/ADR-115.md) clause 1 rather than written. **`0048` stays free.**

**THE SECOND FINDING WOULD HAVE SHIPPED AND IT REFUSES A PURCHASE.** `identity_signals` carries its natural key as a `CREATE UNIQUE INDEX` ([`0002:134`](../packages/db/migrations/0002_identity.sql)), and [ADR-112](decisions/ADR-112.md)'s `uniqueKeys()` reads four sources of which an index is none, so `{ kind, valueHash }` cannot address a write and the obvious blind insert raises `23505` on **the second purchase by any returning trader**. Inside checkout's transaction Postgres turns that `COMMIT` into a `ROLLBACK`, which is enrichment blocking a checkout through the database rather than through a decision. The write is a `rowsWhere` then an `updateAt` addressed by `id`, and **the residual race two concurrent checkouts by one identity leave open is named with the two constructions that close it**, an `ON CONFLICT` upsert or a savepoint, both diffs on [`scoped-db.ts`](../packages/db/src/scoped-db.ts) and both outside this fence. **[ADR-102](decisions/ADR-102.md) foreclosed nested transactions because no caller existed. A caller exists now, and this is that report.**

**NON-BLOCKING IS A TYPE RATHER THAN A PROMISE.** `observeEnrichment` returns `Promise<void>`, so a call site has nothing to branch on, and it never throws, because a throw inside checkout's transaction is a rollback and a propagating enrichment failure is enforcement by exception, which is a SILENT decline of the kind ADR-023 forbids even in step 3. `test/no-authority.test.ts` asserts the five source properties that make the three watched failure directions exhaustive rather than sampled, and it strips comments before it greps so the explanations can stay in the file.

**NO ENABLED CONTRACT ROW MEANS NO CALL AT ALL.** The row is installed `enabled: false` with `approved_by` and `approved_at` as required parameters, because "an enabled contract with no approver is a disclosure nobody authorised". `integration` names the ROLE and `event_name` names the MOMENT, which is [M03 section 7.9.1](plans/M03-billing-checkout.md)'s one vendor and two moments. The `integration_dispatches` row is written **whenever the subject left Merit, including on a timeout**, because a vendor that received a buyer's email and then failed to answer received it exactly as much as one that answered.

**THE CALL SITE IS OWED AND NOT INVENTED.** `apps/api/src/routes/checkout.ts` is session **220**'s and had not landed on `origin/main` when this branch closed. It is not created and not stubbed; the package is complete and unwired, which is an honest deliverable where a checkout route written by the wrong session is a collision that costs two branches.

**Measured on this branch rather than inherited.** Seven source files, five suites, **83 assertions**; full suite **134 files / 2,244 passed / 1 skipped** to **139 files / 2,327 passed / 1 skipped**; **seven seeds watched failing and all seven removed**; invariants **9 of 9**, gates **30 of 30**, `pnpm run verify` exit 0. The package declares **no runtime and no workspace dependency**, reaches `node:crypto` and nothing else, and [`pnpm-lock.yaml`](../pnpm-lock.yaml) gains **+12 lines and 0 deletions**, which is [`packages/psp`](../packages/psp/package.json)'s measured figure exactly.

## `RI-10` covers `scripts/` now, and the workflow line that was told to move did not (2026-08-27, session 233)

**`scripts/demo/` named `.js` files that are `.ts` at 32 sites across 7 files, and `node --experimental-strip-types scripts/demo/main.ts` died with `ERR_MODULE_NOT_FOUND` on its own first relative import.** Reproduced against `origin/main` at `421e52e` before any branch was blamed. Every gate in this repository was green over it, [`RI-10`](../packages/tooling/checks/repo-invariants.mjs) included, because `RI-10` was scoped to `src/`. The `.mjs` wrappers register [`ts-resolve.mjs`](../scripts/demo/ts-resolve.mjs), which maps the extension the tolerant way, and Vitest resolves the same tolerant way, so both suites in `scripts/demo/test/` passed over a tree the node loader could not load.

**THE SCOPING DECISION WAS THE FINDING AND THE SPECIFIERS WERE TRANSCRIPTION.** [ADR-121](decisions/ADR-121.md), `status: proposed`, approval line UNSIGNED, **not a money path by subject**. It fixes what "shipped source" means: the directories `node --experimental-strip-types` loads, which is `src/` under `apps/` or `packages/` **plus everything under `scripts/`**, minus the segment `test/`. It has never meant *published*; `scripts/demo` ships to nobody and is covered anyway, because coverage follows the loader.

**THE SIMPLIFICATION THAT LOOKS FREE WAS MEASURED AND REFUSED, AND THAT IS THE HALF A LATER SESSION WILL WANT TO REVERSE.** Dropping the `src/` clause and scanning every non-`test/` TypeScript file under the three areas finds **the same 19 findings and nothing else**, so re-measuring it will make it look free every time. It is not: it silently admits `apps/portal/e2e/slop-score.spec.ts` and `apps/site/e2e/slop-score.spec.ts`, which are Playwright specs, which are tests, which the ruling puts out of scope. Keeping them out costs a second name in the subtraction, and **a subtraction that grows by name is the failure `RI-10`'s own history is about**: its first draft excluded a package BY NAME and the `src/` line was the principled repair of that.

**THE RESERVED COUNT WAS WRONG AND IS SUPERSEDED.** The dispatch and the `nightly.yml` comment both said 16. Measured: **19 broken specifiers across 5 non-test files, 32 across 7 with the two Vitest suites.** Every site was checked against disk before it was rewritten, because session 148's blanket `.js` to `.ts` rewrite broke [`packages/eslint-plugin-merit/index.js`](../packages/eslint-plugin-merit/index.js), which is genuine JavaScript; 32 rewritten, **0 left ambiguous**.

**THE WIDENED CHECK WAS WATCHED FAILING BEFORE IT WAS BELIEVED PASSING**, because `RI-10` once shipped a `ReferenceError` that could only fire on a real finding and seeding is what caught it. Three rows: a `.js` specifier under `scripts/` that must FAIL, the same defect inside `scripts/demo/test/` that must NOT fire, and a `scripts/` specifier naming a genuine `.js` file that must NOT fire. **The first was confirmed load-bearing** by reverting the scope and watching only that row go red.

**`nightly.yml` CARRIED A STANDING INSTRUCTION TO MOVE `CI-09`'s REPLAY LINE TO THE `.ts` ENTRY ONCE THE SWEEP LANDED, AND THE LINE DID NOT MOVE.** The instruction's premise was that the broken specifiers were why the leg ran `seed-world.mjs`; the sweep disproved it. **`node --experimental-strip-types scripts/demo/seed-world.ts` exits 0 and writes ZERO BYTES**: it exports `main` and never invokes it, and the `.mjs` wrapper is what registers the hook, wires `argv` and stdio, calls `main` and returns its code, exactly as [`run.mjs`](../scripts/demo/run.mjs)'s header has said since it was written. **Moving the line would have replaced a self-audit that reports with a module-graph load that cannot, and CI would have gone green on it**, which is `FM-17`'s shape and which `seed-world.ts`'s own refusal handling names. The `run:` line is byte-identical and only its comment changed, because the sentence it carried is false after this branch.

**Two gaps are written down rather than closed.** `.mjs` files are read by no specifier check here, and closing that needs a reader that understands string context, because [`scripts/ci/falsify-ci.mjs`](../scripts/ci/falsify-ci.mjs) carries `import ... from './scoped-db.js'` inside string literals, which is the exact trap `RI-10`'s second draft fell into. And `RI-10` has no "inspected zero files" guard; the obvious version would be furniture, because `apps/` and `packages/` keep the count non-zero whether or not `scripts/` still exists.
